item.title: Bond yields push higher as investors digest global risks, higher-for-longer path for the Fed
item.author: Jake Conley
item.description:
Bond yields push higher as investors digest global risks, higher-for-longer path for the Fed
2026-09-29
Por Jake Conley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bond-yields-push-higher-as-investors-digest-global-risks-higher-for-longer-path-for-the-fed-183719554.html
Yields on the longer end of the curve rose further to multidecade highs on Monday as a bond sell-off deepened.
The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX), often referred to as the most critical number in global finance for its widespread use as a benchmark rate, advanced roughly 5 basis points to 5.25%, its highest level since 2007, when yields rose in the run-up to the Great Financial Crisis.
Further out on the curve, 30-year Treasury yields (^TYX) advanced by 6 basis points to 5.57%, a level not touched since 2004. The short end was also under pressure, as the 2-year yield (2YY=F) rose by roughly 8 basis points to 4.93%.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
Bets on further rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, an energy crisis kicked off by the war in Iran, ballooning US government debt and budget deficits, and a historic investment cycle driven by the AI build-out have all contributed to a sell-off that has spooked investors.
Of those concerns, the Federal Reserve is perhaps the biggest focus for investors. Earlier in September, the Fed issued a quarter-point rate hike, raising the US target lending rate for the first time in three years.
"We now have data broadly defined that says the economy has indeed strengthened," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said in a press conference following the meeting. "Underlying growth is higher. Inflation is the problem. Stable prices have been the problem for now more than five and a half years."
More notable than the hike itself, however, were projections indicating that a majority of voting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members expected at least another quarter-point hike, reinforcing a higher-for-longer outlook for rates. Four FOMC members saw the need for the Fed to hike rates by 50 basis points in 2026.
The FOMC's price stability mandate has pushed the Fed to raise rates, per Warsh's statement. The war in Iran has made that mandate more consequential as it pushes up energy prices around the globe, increasing strain on businesses and consumers.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
The AI boom has added another source of upward pressure.
A surge in spending on data centers, chips, power generation, and other infrastructure has helped keep US investment and economic growth resilient, even as financing costs have climbed. That strength can push yields higher by reducing the case for lower interest rates, while the enormous capital requirements of the build-out are adding to "competition for capital," or the demand for financing across the economy.

Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
The AI boom has added another source of upward pressure.
A surge in spending on data centers, chips, power generation, and other infrastructure has helped keep US investment and economic growth resilient, even as financing costs have climbed. That strength can push yields higher by reducing the case for lower interest rates, while the enormous capital requirements of the build-out are adding to "competition for capital," or the demand for financing across the economy.

item.title: Why diesel price and Treasury yield relief would be huge wins for stocks
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why diesel price and Treasury yield relief would be huge wins for stocks
2026-09-29
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/why-diesel-price-and-treasury-yield-relief-would-be-huge-wins-for-stocks-123039493.html
If there is relief to be had from surging gas prices and rising Treasury yields soon, it could open the door for another thrust higher for the market.
That's a big if, but it's one to keep an eye on just like the power brokers on Wall Street.
"While AI strength has kept the headline S&P 500 relatively resilient, the median stock in the index trades 16% below its 52-week high, dragging market breadth to its lowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble," Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider said. "Together, these factors indicate the potential for both broad market upside and a 'catch-up' from recent laggards if macro uncertainty declines."
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) continues to trade near record highs despite elevated oil prices and surging bond yields, underpinned by robust corporate earnings growth this year.
Analysts project aggregate third quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of nearly 29% year over year, providing a strong fundamental floor that absorbs elevated discount rates.
Further helping the S&P 500 is the return of the "Magnificent Seven" trade amid AI optimism, which has lit a renewed flame under names like Meta (META) and Nvidia (NVDA).
Outside of the AI complex, that's where things get hairy for the S&P 500, as there are a host of laggards.
McDonald's (MCD), PepsiCo (PEP), Lowe's (LOW), and Nike (NKE) are all hovering around 52-week lows.
Goldman's Snider is banking on improved market breadth supporting a higher S&P 500 in the next 12 months. He expects the S&P 500 to rise 13% to 8,700 over that span.

item.title: China and US pledge tariff cuts
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
China and US pledge tariff cuts
2026-09-28
Por Texto propio
China, US pledge tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods including agriculture, toys, toasters
Liz Lee · September 28, 2026 · reuters.com
BEIJING, Sept 28 (Reuters) - China and the United States said they will pursue tariff cuts on $60 billion worth ‌of goods imported from each other, including products from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese toys to household appliances, with some notable omissions on each side.
Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday night.
For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% of US exports to China, he said.
The reciprocal tariff reduction effort as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week.
But statements from neither side indicated the extent of tariff reductions nor any timing for implementation. USTR said the $30 billion valuation for import product lists proposed by ⁠each country were based on 2024 import data.
One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties, opens new tab on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. But it excluded non-seed soybeans, the biggest US agricultural export to China, which totaled $16.2 billion in 2025.
The American Soybean Association expressed disappointment at the exclusion, saying Beijing's 10% retaliatory tariff would keep Chinese purchases of US soybeans controlled by state-directed enterprises.
"Removing the tariff would improve the competitiveness of US soybeans and provide greater opportunity for private Chinese buyers," the trade group said.
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures plunged on Monday, reflecting traders' disappointment at the announcement and the unwinding of a buildup of net long positions in soybean futures.
But Beijing will look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices, according to the Chinese list.
In another list were Washington's proposed reciprocal tariff cuts, opens new tab for Chinese consumer goods, including small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens.
The broad category for toys, including children's bicycles, topped the US list, totaling $14.4 billion in 2024 but falling to $9.8 billion in 2025 amid Trump's higher tariffs, according to US Census Bureau data. The US list also included Chinese fireworks, artificial flowers, holiday decorations and children’s car seats.
LONGER TRADE TRUCE
Item 1 of 3 Workers stack empty shipping containers for storage at Wando Welch Terminal operated by the South Carolina Ports Authority in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, U.S. May 10, 2018. Picture taken May 10, 2018. REUTERS/Randall Hill
Workers stack empty shipping containers for storage at Wando Welch Terminal operated by the South Carolina Ports Authority in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, U.S. May 10, 2018. Picture taken May 10, 2018. REUTERS/Randall Hill Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab
China's commerce ministry said ‌on Monday ⁠a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to January 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts.
The extension also provides a "relatively stable and predictable policy environment" for cooperation among companies and continued active discussions.
Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises' concerns, the ministry
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: 3 tech stock charts you probably won't believe
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
3 tech stock charts you probably won't believe
2026-09-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/3-tech-stock-charts-you-probably-wont-believe-133326724.html
Tech stocks are having a September to remember.
Meta's (META) Muse AI agent has burst onto the scene, powering the company's stock and the "Magnificent Seven" complex to boot. However, former Trump economic adviser Gary Cohn isn't all in on Muse, as he said on Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed.
Chip giant AMD (AMD) officially crossed above the $1 trillion mark for the first time. The achievement made CEO Lisa Su the first inductee into the Sozzi Unleashed Wall of Titans.
And when memory chip play Micron (MU) reports earnings this week, analysts are expecting a huge quarter and outlook in the face of the AI boom. That will go a long way toward reinforcing the very bullish Wall Street calls on Micron this month.
But you wouldn't understand the excitement of the current tech moment by looking at valuations in the space. Truist chief market strategist Keith Lerner served up a few tech charts that will get you thinking.
Chart 1: Cheap tech valuations
Tech stock valuations are back to levels seen when OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) launched ChatGPT.
Chart 2: Tech earnings are blowing other sectors away
There is tech, and there is everybody else in the S&P 500 (^IXIC). The valuation compression in tech almost makes no sense given the sector's strong earnings outlook.
Chart 3: The tech stock relative disconnect
Tech's premium relative to the broader market is near bull-market lows, believe it or not.

item.title: MongoDB stock tanks after Meta poaches CEO
item.author: Michael B Kelley
item.description:
MongoDB stock tanks after Meta poaches CEO
2026-09-28
Por Michael B Kelley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/mongodb-stock-tanks-after-meta-poaches-ceo-132048225.html
MongoDB (MDB) stock is falling after Meta (META) hired MongoDB CEO Chirantan "CJ" Desai to lead the new Meta Enterprise Platform.
"Meta Enterprise Platform will use our strengths that few other companies have: advanced models, leading agents, large-scale infrastructure, and years of working closely with many businesses," Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated in a press release. "Initially, we will focus on bringing our full technology stack, including the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to businesses and developers to help them grow."
Read more: Meta's Muse is an impressively capable AI agent, despite some hiccups
MongoDB addressed the departure, naming company veteran Dev Ittycheria as interim president and CEO. Ittycheria served as president and CEO MongoDB, which provides servers and a platform to help enterprises store and manage large amounts of data, from 2014 to 2025.
"MongoDB's business is strong, and there is no better person to take on the role of President and CEO in the interim than Dev Ittycheria," Tom Killalea, chairman of the board of directors, stated in a press release. "He knows this company deeply, has remained an involved and active executive board member over the past year, and will step in immediately to ensure a seamless transition."
In a note to clients, Guggenheim Securities analysts described the move as "a real shocker to us considering a few factors: 1) CJ has been at the company for less than a year, 2) he has been the main spokesperson for the company with regards to MongoDB's suitability for agentic development to customers, partners, investors, and 3) MongoDB's annual investor day is tomorrow."
The note added that the "only slight positive news is that former CEO Dev Ittycheria will reassume the role of President and CEO for now—there is no one that is better suited to run MongoDB, in our view. However, Mr. Ittycheria was clear about his retirement plans, so he will likely be looking for an appropriate successor soon, and hopefully he will stay on longer to pass along his invaluable institutional knowledge."

item.title: María Paz Jervis renuncia a la Presidencia de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción
item.author: Patricia González
item.description:
María Paz Jervis renuncia a la Presidencia de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción
2026-09-28
Por Patricia González
https://www.primicias.ec/economia/empresas/maria-paz-jervis-renuncia-presidencia-camara-industrias-produccion-cip-empresas-miedo-133625/
María Paz Jervis renuncia a la Presidencia de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción
La renuncia de María Paz Jervis se da luego de la celebración de los 90 años de la CIP, en la que alertó que "pocas veces había visto un sector empresarial con tanto miedo".
María Paz Jervis da un discurso como presidenta de la CIP, en el Aniversario 90 del gremio, el 24 de septiembre de 2026. Imagen referencial.
- Foto
CIP / X
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
María-Paz Jervis renunció a la Presidencia Ejecutiva de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción (CIP), informaron Jervis y el gremio en la red social X, este 28 de septiembre.
"Hoy concluyo mi etapa como Presidenta Ejecutiva de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción. Han sido cuatro años de aprendizajes, desafíos y, sobre todo, de recorrer el país y conocer de cerca la importancia de su sector productivo", escribió Jervis.
Por su parte, la CIP informó en un comunicado que aceptó la renuncia de Jervis a la Presidencia Ejecutiva del gremio y le agradeció "por su trabajo y dedicación durante su gestión".
"La Cámara mantiene su carácter gremial e independiente. Continuaremos trabajando con responsabilidad y firmeza por un entorno que favorezca la inversión, la producción, el empleo y el desarrollo del país", añadió el gremio.
Discurso polémico
La renuncia de Jervis se da luego de la celebración de los 90 años de la CIP, que tuvo lugar el jueves 24 de septiembre, en Quito.
En su discurso, la entonces Presidenta del la Cámara alertó que "pocas veces había visto un sector empresarial con tanto miedo", desesperanza y resignación. "Estoy segura que hay muchas cosas que cambiar en el país, el decirlo no nos convierte en enemigos de nadie", señaló.
Jervis también se solidarizo con el gremio periodístico del país, ante las actuales circunstancias que atraviesan algunos periodistas y medios en el país, como Diario Expreso: "Me resulta incomprensible el silencio ante la persecución de periodistas, ante el acoso a medios de comunicación. En democracia, esto no debería ocurrir".

María Paz Jervis renuncia a la Presidencia de la Cámara de Industrias y Producción

item.title: ¿Quién es Bernardo Cordovez, el nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo de Ecuador?
item.author: Santiago Sarango
item.description:
¿Quién es Bernardo Cordovez, el nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo de Ecuador?
2026-09-28
Por Santiago Sarango
https://www.primicias.ec/economia/trayectoria-bernardo-cordovez-nuevo-ministro-economia-decreto509-amenaza-iess-133579/
¿Quién es Bernardo Cordovez, el nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo de Ecuador?
El nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo ha ocupado varios cargos en el sector público desde 2025. Durante su gestión en el IESS, denunció haber recibido una amenaza.
Fotografía de archivo de Bernardo Cordovez, nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo.
- Foto
@BernardoCordovz
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Con el Decreto Ejecutivo 509, el presidente Daniel Noboa designó a Bernardo Cordovez como nuevo ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo, en reemplazo de Sariha Moya.
Cordovez estuvo durante 10 meses como representante del Ejecutivo en el Consejo Directivo del Instituto Ecuatoriano de Seguridad Social (IESS).
Durante ese período, el funcionario recorrió varias casas de salud para evaluar su funcionamiento y conocer de primera mano las necesidades de los pacientes y afiliados del IESS respecto a la atención que recibían.
Una amenaza en medio de su gestión en el IESS
En marzo de 2026, Cordovez denunció una presunta amenaza en su contra, que atribuyó a una banda criminal.
“Los Tiguerones mandamos aquí”, decía el mensaje.
Cordovez no dio más detalles sobre la amenaza, como el lugar exacto donde fue encontrada o quién la recibió. Sin embargo, aseguró que no cedería ni negociaría ante quienes buscan “imponer el caos en los hospitales”.
Nuevo rol en el Gobierno
Bernardo Cordovez llegó al Consejo Directivo del IESS en noviembre de 2025, en reemplazo de Edgar Lama.
Ahora, en menos de un año, asumirá un nuevo cargo dentro del Gobierno de Daniel Noboa, esta vez al frente del Ministerio de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo.
De acuerdo con la información sobre su formación profesional registrada en la Secretaría de Educación Superior, Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación (Senescyt), Cordovez tiene una maestría en Dirección Financiera con mención en Mercado de Valores, de la Universidad Espíritu Santo, y una licenciatura en Administración Financiera por el Instituto Tecnológico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey.
Antes de asumir su nuevo cargo, Cordovez ocupó los siguientes puestos dentro de la función pública:
- Asesor 2 en el Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas: abril de 2025
- Gerente General del BIESS: mayo de 2025
- Presidente del Consejo Directivo del IESS: noviembre de 2025
- Ministro de Desarrollo Económico y Productivo: septiembre de 2026

item.title: Con custodia narcoparamilitar y entre hoteles, así vivían la hija y la esposa de alias 'Fito' en Colombia
item.author: Karla Pesantes
item.description:
Con custodia narcoparamilitar y entre hoteles, así vivían la hija y la esposa de alias 'Fito' en Colombia
2026-09-28
Por Karla Pesantes
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/michelle-macias-inda-penarrieta-custodia-narcoparamilitar-hija-esposa-alias-fito-colombia-133587/
Con custodia narcoparamilitar y entre hoteles, así vivían la hija y la esposa de alias 'Fito' en Colombia
Michelle Macías e Inda Mariela Peñarrieta, hija y esposa del narco ecuatoriano alias 'Fito', estuvieron en Venezuela antes de radicarse en Santander, Colombia. Fueron encontradas con más de USD 10.000 en efectivo.
Momentos de la detención de Michelle Macías, hija de alias 'Fito', y de Inda Peñarrieta, esposa del narco ecuatoriano, Santander, Colombia, el 27 de septiembre de 2026.
- Foto
Cortesía Dirección General de Investigación de Ecuador
Autor:
redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Con apoyo de la agencia FBI de Estados Unidos, la Policía de Colombia detuvo a la esposa y una hija de Adolfo Macías, alias Fito, el máximo líder de Los Choneros, quienes se escondían desde hace meses en Santander.
Las mujeres detenidas se llaman Inda Mariela Peñarrieta y Michelle Macías, esposa e hija, respectivamente del narco ecuatoriana, y son requeridas por la justicia ecuatoriana acusadas de lavado de activos por más de USD 25 millones.
El operativo de detención de las dos mujeres contó también con la Unidad Nacional contra Estructuras Criminales Complejas (UNECC) de Ecuador que coordinó y lideró la intervención en Colombia.
Alias 'Fito', por su parte', está preso en Estados Unidos luego de que Ecuador lo extraditó y enfrenta cargos por narcotráfico y tráfico de armas, con penas de entre 20 años de prisión y cadena perpetua.
Cuando fueron detenidas ambas mujeres, el presidente colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella señaló que Peñarrieta y su hija fueron encontradas en su vivienda en Sabana de Torres, un municipio de Santander ubicado al noreste del país.
Según un documento oficial al que tuvo acceso PRIMICIAS, para llegar hasta Colombia, ambas mujeres salieron primero desde Ecuador rumbo a Venezuela.
Luego ingresaron vía terrestre a Colombia, llegaron en primera instancia a Bogotá y después pasaron a Bucaramanga, donde vivieron tres meses y 20 días, es decir, hasta su captura.
Otro detalle del lugar donde vivían la esposa e hija de alias 'Fito' es que estaban escondidas en un sector manejado por el ELN y por el grupo narcoparamilitar Los Conquistadores, de acuerdo con el documento oficial.
"La familia siempre le preocupó a él (alias Fito) y buscaron este sector (Santander), donde entiendo funcionan ciertos grupos irregulares, quienes estaban a cargo quizás de la seguridad de esas señoras", dijo el ministro del Interior, John Reimberg, en entrevista con el canal Caracol, este 28 de septiembre, tras la captura de ambas mujeres.
Este grupo irregular al que hace mención Reimberg sería las Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada (ACSN), responsables de la reciente ola de atentados en la turística ciudad colombiana de Santa Marta.
Según Reimberg, la supuesta relación de alias 'Fito' con el expresidente colombiano Gustavo Petro facilitó que los familiares del narco ecuatoriano ingresen al país con identidades falsas.
En otra entrevista con el medio colombiano Blu Radio, Reimberg adelantó que la Embajada ecuatoriana ya tomó contacto con las autoridades de Colombia y que "se trabaja de manera conjunta para concretar el traslado" de Macías y Peñarrieta. Se prevé que dicha extradición a Ecuador ocurra en unos dos días.
Pagaban en efectivo y vivían en hoteles
A raíz de la expulsión de Michelle Macías y de Inda Peñarrieta de Argentina en 2024, la Policía de Ecuador rastreó los constantes desplazamientos de las dos familiares de alias 'Fito'.
Y en este monitoreo, las autoridades notaron que las dos habían pasado por varias ciudades colombianas entre 2023 y 2024.
Luego en 2025, luego de la recaptura de alias 'Fito' en su búnker, ambas mujeres salier

Otro detalle del lugar donde vivían la esposa e hija de alias 'Fito' es que estaban escondidas en un sector manejado por el ELN y por el grupo narcoparamilitar Los Conquistadores, de acuerdo con el documento oficial.
"La familia siempre le preocupó a él (alias Fito) y buscaron este sector (Santander), donde entiendo funcionan ciertos grupos irregulares, quienes estaban a cargo quizás de la seguridad de esas señoras", dijo el ministro del Interior, John Reimberg, en entrevista con el canal Caracol, este 28 de septiembre, tras la captura de ambas mujeres.
Este grupo irregular al que hace mención Reimberg sería las Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada (ACSN), responsables de la reciente ola de atentados en la turística ciudad colombiana de Santa Marta.
Según Reimberg, la supuesta relación de alias 'Fito' con el expresidente colombiano Gustavo Petro facilitó que los familiares del narco ecuatoriano ingresen al país con identidades falsas.
En otra entrevista con el medio colombiano Blu Radio, Reimberg adelantó que la Embajada ecuatoriana ya tomó contacto con las autoridades de Colombia y que "se trabaja de manera conjunta para concretar el traslado" de Macías y Peñarrieta. Se prevé que dicha extradición a Ecuador ocurra en unos dos días.
Pagaban en efectivo y vivían en hoteles
A raíz de la expulsión de Michelle Macías y de Inda Peñarrieta de Argentina en 2024, la Policía de Ecuador rastreó los constantes desplazamientos de las dos familiares de alias 'Fito'.
Y en este monitoreo, las autoridades notaron que las dos habían pasado por varias ciudades colombianas entre 2023 y 2024.
Luego en 2025, luego de la recaptura de alias 'Fito' en su búnker, ambas mujeres salier

item.title: Fiscalía y registros judiciales esbozan nexos de la red de Mocolí con drogas en cargamentos de banano, aunque no apuntan al CJNG
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
Fiscalía y registros judiciales esbozan nexos de la red de Mocolí con drogas en cargamentos de banano, aunque no apuntan al CJNG
2026-09-28
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/red-mocoli-jalisco-fiscalia-indicios-relacion-internacional-133450/
Fiscalía y registros judiciales esbozan nexos de la red de Mocolí con drogas en cargamentos de banano, aunque no apuntan al CJNG
La Fiscalía imputó por delincuencia organizada a 36 personas tras los operativos ejecutados con apoyo de Estados Unidos. Según el Ministerio del Interior, se trata de una estructura presuntamente vinculada al Cartel Jalisco Nueva Generación. Documentos judiciales describen una logística que estaría relacionada con la contaminación de contenedores de banano con droga.
Uno de los detenidos en Guayas el 24 de septiembre de 2026, en un operativo ejecutado por la Policía de Ecuador y el Comando Sur de Estados Unidos.
- Foto
Policía Nacional
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
La madrugada del 24 de septiembre de 2026, el Ministerio del Interior anunció el desmantelamiento de una estructura criminal en cuatro provincias del Ecuador, involucrada en el tráfico de más de seis toneladas de cocaína.
La intervención contó con la cooperación de la DEA y efectivos del Comando Sur de Estados Unidos. El ministro John Reimberg señaló que se trató de un golpe directo a una célula presuntamente vinculada al Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), luego de ocho meses de investigación.
En la audiencia de formulación de cargos, el 25 de septiembre, la Fiscalía formalizó el caso por delincuencia organizada sin presentar elementos sobre una supuesta alianza de los detenidos con un cartel mexicano.
La imputación se sustentó en escuchas telefónicas, seguimientos y cinco decomisos ejecutados durante la investigación previa. Los expedientes judiciales de los procesados exponen una red con antecedentes locales.
¿Hay rastro del CJNG?
El despliegue de las fuerzas ecuatorianas y estadounidenses se realizó la madrugada del 24 de septiembre de 2026 en Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos y El Oro. La operación movilizó a 320 policías ecuatorianos y 50 militares del Comando Sur de Estados Unidos durante el toque de queda vigente.
John Reimberg, ministro del Interior, afirmó que la red respondía de forma directa al Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación. Según su versión, la organización recibía droga desde Colombia y la enviaba a Estados Unidos y Europa.
El presidente Daniel Noboa también destacó el golpe en sus redes sociales. La vocería oficial sostuvo que el operativo causó un perjuicio económico al narcotráfico estimado en USD 322 millones tras las incautaciones continuadas de sustancias ilícitas.
En el impulso fiscal previo presentado a las 23:15 del 24 de septiembre de 2026 no se recogió esa tesis. El fiscal José Bravo Salazar solicitó la audiencia de formulación de cargos por el presunto delito de delincuencia organizada.
Asimismo, en el expediente no se recogieron indicios sobre la relación de los ahora procesados con una organización criminal mexicana. La imputación se centró en probar una confabulación entre los 36 detenidos para el acopio y transporte terrestre de cocaína.
Durante la diligencia judicial, la defensora pública Francoise Rhon objetó la acusación. La abogada sostuvo ante el juez que una etiqueta policial no constituye una conducta típica si no se demuestran los actos individuales de cada uno.
La defensora cuestionó que la Fiscalía no precisó quién financiaba, quién daba las órdenes ni quién contaminaba los contenedores. El argumento enfatizó que las reuniones o llamadas no pueden criminalizarse sin pruebas directas de que se cometió un delito.
Documentos de causas previas iniciadas contra miembros de esta red no hacen referencia a estructuras criminales mexicanas, pero sí a actividades ilícitas en Ecuador y a drogas. En el proceso 17U05-2026-00047, iniciado por la incautación de más de dos toneladas de cocaína en Babahoyo, ya había sido investigado
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.author: Carlos Rojas

Por Carlos Rojas
https://www.ecuavisa.com/codigo-rojas/golpes-reimberg-son-gran-utilidad-20260924-0080.html
El relato de John Reimberg debe retener la mayor cantidad de oxÃgeno para apuntalar la popularidad del oficialismo de cara a las elecciones del 29 de noviembre y proyectar la imagen de un gobierno eficiente en la lucha criminal, por encima de lo demÃ¡s. Â
Bajo ningÃºn punto de vista se puede minimizar el operativo contra una red del Cartel Jalisco Nueva GeneraciÃ³n que cayÃ³ en isla MocolÃ y otras ciudades de la costa. Y menos, luego del reporte del ministro del Interior, John Reinberg, del que se desprenden varios puntos fundamentales que no se pueden obviar.
El primero de ellos, que este grupo narcoterrorista mexicano opera en Ecuador de manera autÃ³noma, sin tener lazos con los GDO locales como lobos, choneros o esas cosas. Aquello constata la profunda vulnerabilidad que tiene el paÃs, ya no como autopista del narcotrÃ¡fico, sino como un verdadero centro de operaciones criminales.
Si el crimen y el terrorismo son transnacionales, las fuerzas democrÃ¡ticas encargadas de combatirlos tambiÃn deben serlo. Por eso, que Reimberg haya confirmado que el Comando Sur participÃ³ en este operativo muestra el grado de inmersiÃ³n de los militares de EE. UU. que, por fuera de las alertas puestas sobre el debate de la soberanÃa o el respeto de los derechos humanos, genera entusiasmo en amplios sectores del Ecuador que esperan el sometimiento de la violencia.
Adicionalmente, estÃ¡ el hecho de que para golpear a estos criminales hubo una investigaciÃ³n de ocho meses. Es decir, el trabajo de las instituciones del Estado, asÃ como de inteligencia, en este caso, ha dado un resultado positivo.
Reimberg, de lejos, es el mejor vocero que tiene el Gobierno y su relato debe retener la mayor cantidad de oxÃgeno posible para que perviva en la opiniÃ³n con dos objetivos fundamentales.
En el fondo, la estrategia polÃtica y comunicacional del RÃgimen tiene como propÃ³sito que la sociedad sienta que la lucha contra el crimen organizado debe ser el alfa y la omega de la discusiÃ³n nacional, asÃ no haya medicinas en los hospitales, vuelvan los apagones, la producciÃ³n petrolera se desplome, no crezcan los puestos de trabajo o, simplemente, no bajen las muertes violentas, que es el gran indicador que nos dirÃ¡ si esta guerra, en verdad, la estamos venciendo.

item.title: US-China summit ends with little progress on trade and AI — other than 2 new deadlines
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
US-China summit ends with little progress on trade and AI — other than 2 new deadlines
2026-09-28
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/us-china-summit-ends-with-little-progress-on-trade-and-ai--other-than-2-new-deadlines-174257772.html
President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping wrapped up a state visit Friday afternoon with another round of events high on choreography but low on progress on trade and artificial intelligence.
Perhaps the most direct takeaway came in the form of two new dates to circle on the calendar.
On AI, a summit in Shenzhen, China, in November was announced to discuss issues like AI safety, which saw little progress this week. Trump posted Friday that he would meet with XI at that summit and said, "Much has been, and will be, accomplished."
On tariffs, an existing trade truce, which was set to expire in November, got a short-term extension to Jan. 10, 2027.
Both moves marked a delay from the US and China in confronting these fundamental issues and came as the two leaders went out of their way to underline the positive relationship between the world's two largest economies.
Trump repeatedly offered lavish praise and said during a tea in the White House's Red Room that it had been "a tremendous visit [with] great strides, very positive, for both countries."
The Chinese leader reciprocated with talk of a friendship between the two nations as the visit ended on Friday at the US National Archives, where Trump and Xi viewed the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution before saying their goodbyes.
Yet the lack of specifics left many policy experts wanting.
Capital Economics wrote in an analysis that, on substantive issues, the visit had offered "little beyond a short reprieve."
"The elaborate welcome and ceremony surrounding President Xi's state visit to the US could not hide the lack of substantive progress," the report said, describing the dynamic underneath the pageantry as "mutual suspicion."
On tariffs, a pause to assess 'whether or not to continue this period of relative peace'
The key headline from the summit for tariff watchers was an announcement on Wednesday that the US and China would extend their current trade truce by two months, with a new early 2027 deadline for trade talks.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that the US and China had also reached agreements to reduce tariffs on a "subset" of nonsensitive goods and that those details would be released on Monday.
Trump's team has said that the coming months could yield a "bigger deal," even as Greer made clear that trade tensions could quickly re-emerge. He described the coming months as a time "to reassess and determine whether or not to continue this period of relative peace on the economic front with the Chinese."
Trump's team is currently considering new 7.5% tariffs on China around the issue of overcapacity. Though an investigation this summer means the new levies could be imposed quickly, they have been delayed — likely until after the midterm elections if not further — in part due to withering US public opinion on tariffs.
Xi, in his remarks, underlined the tenuous nature of the truce. He said he wanted to increase cooperation and trade with the US, but only if "two sides uphold the spirit of equality, mutual respect, and mutual benefit."
The truce, first announced in South Korea last October, included provisions suspending some tariffs and promises from the Chinese government regarding rare earth exports.
AI safety summit later this fall
The main advancement in AI took the form of plans for a "notification mechanism" to increase communication between two nations in the event of AI incidents.
The Chinese have been silent on whether they will embrace the idea, but US Ambassador to China David Perdue said on Fox News on Friday that this new channel of communication was moving forward and would be significant even amid questions about how it would work.
"We

item.title: Goldman Sachs says 80% of ultra-rich investors are fleeing stocks for alternative assets — and it's not bonds
item.author: Vawn Himmelsbach
item.description:
Goldman Sachs says 80% of ultra-rich investors are fleeing stocks for alternative assets — and it's not bonds
2026-09-28
Por Vawn Himmelsbach
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-sachs-says-80-ultra-111500026.html
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.
Stocks have been on a tear recently. The S&P 500 has repeatedly hit record highs over the past couple of months, despite concerns over geopolitical turmoil, rising bond yields and some U.S. economic policies.
Still, some market observers see warning signs of potential weakness.
JPMorgan sees gold hitting $5,000/oz by Q4 — and savvy investors are protecting their wealth with a tax-advantaged Gold IRA. Get your free guide from Priority Gold
Despite the S&P 500 being close to its all-time high as a whole, Morningstar points out that nearly 60% of individual stocks on the index were actually down 20% or more from their all-time highs (1) in August. They also highlight the current volatility of stock prices, with many moving up and down by as much as 20% in just a few months.
Amid the uncertainty and volatility, current stock market conditions may have you wondering whether you should lighten your stock holdings. And if so, where should you invest the proceeds?
For many investors, selling stocks has typically meant moving the proceeds to bonds. Indeed, for those maintaining a portfolio such as the traditional 60/40 weighting of equities to bonds, the current run-up in stock prices and fall in bond prices could mandate a rebalance in this direction to maintain that weighting.
However, some evidence suggests bonds no longer hedge equities (2) — meaning that some investors might start considering how to allocate some of their portfolio to other asset classes.
One move they're making? A growing number of individual investors are adopting alternative assets. According to a survey by Goldman Sachs (3), 39% of individuals with $1 million to $5 million in investable assets are turning to alternatives. That number grows to 80% for those with assets of $10 million or more.
Indeed, about half (49%) of advisors say they're allocating more than 10% of client portfolios to alternatives (4), according to the 2025 CAIS Mercer Survey.
But you don't need to be an ultra-high-net-worth investor to benefit from investing in alternative assets. Here's how to follow their lead and get a foot in the door:
Add precious metals to your portfolio with a gold IRA
Gold is a classic example of a "strategic" asset (5) in a well-diversified portfolio. That's because gold prices tend to behave differently than stock or bond prices, providing diversification across asset classes and stability during geopolitical and market turmoil.
For instance, gold prices rose dramatically after the 2008 global financial crisis (6). Likewise, the price of gold hit $2,000 per ounce for the first time in history (7) during the COVID-19 pandemic — although current prices (8) are more than double that figure.
Beyond market concerns, inflation remains an ongoing issue. Over the past several years, inflation has remained stubbornly elevated (9).
Gold can be a valuable addition to a portfolio in this environment, since it has historically been treated as a long-term hedge against inflation — particularly when it's used as part of a broader inflation-hedging portfolio.
Holding gold as a tangible asset also protects you from other factors that could impact individual stock valuations, such as earnings, financial leverage and competitive positioning.
If you're new to alternative assets, buying and selling physical gold may seem daunting, but you have a few options. For instance, Priority Gold is a U.S.-based precious metals dealer with an A+ rating from the Better Business Bureau and a 5-star rating from Trust Link.
Beyond directly purchasing gold, you can also convert an existing IRA into a gold IRA — a specialized individual retirement acc

item.title: Oil prices spike after Trump rejects Iran truce offer
item.author: AFP
item.description:
Oil prices spike after Trump rejects Iran truce offer
2026-09-28
Por AFP
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-prices-spike-trump-rejects-034903535.html
Oil prices spiked with bond yields Monday as Donald Trump's rejection of an Iranian offer of a seven-day truce stoked inflation concerns, while stocks were mixed as traders look ahead to the release of key US data.
Tehran last week set out a plan at the UN General Assembly for a halt in hostilities that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened, which would ease a crippling supply crisis that has jacked up costs around the world.
The waterway is key to the world's energy supply and is now central to the conflict between the US and Iran, particularly with Houthis seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping lane.
However, the US president told reporters outside the White House "I reject their proposal".
Still, he told Axios that he expects negotiations to resume.
"They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make," he told the news platform. "It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago."
"They overplayed their hand," Trump added, in the interview published Sunday.
Citing sources familiar with the matter, Axios reported that indirect talks between Washington and Tehran could take place as early as Monday.
Iran was still standing by its conditions for reopening the Strait, including the release of frozen assets, the lifting of sanctions on its oil and an end to the US naval blockade.
Oil prices, which fell more than two percent Friday on news of the offer, bounced back at the start of the new week, with Brent surging more than three percent back above $107 a barrel.
That stoked inflation concerns again, and weighed on stock markets.
Seoul 2.7 percent as it reopened after a long break, while Tokyo, Shanghai, Manila, Mumbai, Bangkok and Jakarta also dropped.
There were gains in Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington, while London, Paris and Frankfurt were also on the front foot.
Bond yields climbed, with the average on a gauge of world bonds topping four percent last week for the first time since 2007, according to Bloomberg.
The rise in prices puts the focus back on the Federal Reserve ahead of its next policy meeting at the end of October, with CME's FedWatch tool putting the chances of a second successive interest rate hike at more than 65 percent.
Before that decision is made, investors will see the release of the bank's preferred gauge of inflation this week as well as a key jobs report that could play a vital role in policymakers' thinking.
"Middle East tensions have flared again after President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz," wrote Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

Still, he told Axios that he expects negotiations to resume.
"They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make," he told the news platform. "It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago."
"They overplayed their hand," Trump added, in the interview published Sunday.
Citing sources familiar with the matter, Axios reported that indirect talks between Washington and Tehran could take place as early as Monday.
Iran was still standing by its conditions for reopening the Strait, including the release of frozen assets, the lifting of sanctions on its oil and an end to the US naval blockade.
Oil prices, which fell more than two percent Friday on news of the offer, bounced back at the start of the new week, with Brent surging more than three percent back above $107 a barrel.
That stoked inflation concerns again, and weighed on stock markets.
Seoul 2.7 percent as it reopened after a long break, while Tokyo, Shanghai, Manila, Mumbai, Bangkok and Jakarta also dropped.
There were gains in Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington, while London, Paris and Frankfurt were also on the front foot.
Bond yields climbed, with the average on a gauge of world bonds topping four percent last week for the first time since 2007, according to Bloomberg.
The rise in prices puts the focus back on the Federal Reserve ahead of its next policy meeting at the end of October, with CME's FedWatch tool putting the chances of a second successive interest rate hike at more than 65 percent.
Before that decision is made, investors will see the release of the bank's preferred gauge of inflation this week as well as a key jobs report that could play a vital role in policymakers' thinking.
"Middle East tensions have flared again after President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz," wrote Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

item.title: SK Hynix Shares Fall as Solidigm’s Potential US IPO Sours Mood
item.author: Youkyung Lee
item.description:
SK Hynix Shares Fall as Solidigm’s Potential US IPO Sours Mood
2026-09-28
Por Youkyung Lee
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sk-hynix-shares-fall-solidigm-031013270.html
(Bloomberg) -- SK Hynix Inc. shares fell as media reports of a potential listing of the chipmaker's US subsidiary added to concerns over its complex ownership structure.
Most Read from Bloomberg
SK Hynix shares dropped 5%, the most in two weeks, after Bloomberg confirmed over the weekend that Solidigm is considering a US initial public offering as soon as next year that could value the data-storage product maker at as much as $100 billion. SK Hynix's biggest holder SK Square Co. tumbled more than 8%, while SK Inc., which controls SK Square, retreated more than 6%.
An IPO of Solidigm would add to the multiple layers of ownership within the group, deepening the pyramid ownership structure, according to the Korea Corporate Governance Forum, a non-profit of investment professionals, which in August urged SK Hynix to drop the plan. SK Hynix owns the NAND memory unit through US subsidiary AI Company, making Solidigm a so-called grandchild company.
"I would be watchful rather than alarmed," said Jung In Yun, chief executive officer at Fibonacci Asset Management Global. "A US listing could unlock Solidigm's value and fund expansion, but SK Hynix shareholders would be giving up a portion of its future earnings."
"The key is the valuation and the use of proceeds," Yun said. "Selling a small stake at an attractive price could create value, while substantial dilution without a convincing investment return would be a concern."
Shares of SK Hynix and other chipmakers, including Samsung Electronics Co., also came under pressure from broader risk-off mood after oil prices rose.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: AI Breaches Add to Safety Fears as Trump Meets Anthropic Chief
item.author: Michael Shepard; Maggie Eastland; Courtney Subramanian
item.description:
AI Breaches Add to Safety Fears as Trump Meets Anthropic Chief
2026-09-28
Por Michael Shepard; Maggie Eastland; Courtney Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-breaches-add-safety-fears-232732405.html
AI Breaches Add to Safety Fears as Trump Meets Anthropic Chief
Michael Shepard, Maggie Eastland and Courtney Subramanian
5 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Global anxiety over artificial intelligence risks has intensified following fresh disclosures about a far wider range of breaches by advanced AI models, setting the stage for a high-stakes meeting between Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and President Donald Trump.
Amodei and Trump were planning to meet Sunday night for dinner, according to people familiar with the matter, bringing together two men at opposite ends of the AI safety debate. The meeting would mark their first private sit-down after months of rocky relations between the Anthropic chief and the administration over safety-related issues involving the company's AI tools.
Trump said Sunday he planned to discuss Amodei's recent calls for slowing down the development pace of new AI models. "We're going to talk about it," he told a reporter on the sidelines of a golf tournament near Chicago. "I'm for, 'Let's go and let's win.'"
Speaking of AI's potential, he added, "It is, in fact, bigger than the internet, and we're leading and we're building trillions of dollars worth of places. And why should we give that up?" Anthropic declined to comment.
The meeting was scheduled against a backdrop of new reports that OpenAI models had carried out unauthorized activity, including the breach of an Australian government system as well as attempts to access dozens of US government and university websites. Late Friday, OpenAI said it would pause training of its most capable models following the discovery that one of its agentic AI systems had escaped a secure testing environment and reached the internet.
Those revelations added to a pile of previous safety incidents disclosed since July by leading AI developers, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms Inc. The episodes have stirred calls for new AI standards from global leaders including United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres, as well as US lawmakers and executives and researchers across the tech industry.
For now, investors on Wall Street are struggling to fit the unfolding safety debate into their calculations about the industry's trajectory. AI infrastructure stocks tumbled following Amodei's essay vowing to pace AI development, over fears such a shift could cut into spending on chips.
Shares recovered after Amodei and Altman stressed that pacing development would not translate into less investment by their companies, both of which are preparing for initial public offerings that could value each business at roughly $1 trillion.
When it comes to AI threats, Amodei and Trump have staked out vastly different positions. The Anthropic chief has long warned about AI's existential risks, and he propelled the safety debate into the mainstream with his Sept. 12 essay, promising to slow development of the most advanced models and urging more regulation. His pledge to pace development was embraced by his rivals, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceXAI founder Elon Musk.
Trump, on the other hand, has belittled those doomsday fears as "a hoax" and rejected calls for more international coordination on AI as "a globalist conspiracy." Following Amodei's essay, Trump launched a string of social media posts opposing new guardrails or any slowdown in AI development — one of which named the Anthropic chief directly — a disagreement that significantly raised the stakes of the Sunday dinner.
Signaling the friction between Anthropic and the administration, Amodei was one of the few high-profile Silicon Valley CEOs to miss Thursday's state dinner at the White House to fete the visiting Chinese leader, Xi Jinping. Those in attendance included
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: US-Greenland Security Deal Opens Door to American Investment
item.author: Isak Hullert
item.description:
US-Greenland Security Deal Opens Door to American Investment
2026-09-28
Por Isak Hullert
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/us-greenland-security-deal-opens-041503601.html
US-Greenland Security Deal Opens Door to American Investment
Isak Hullert
4 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Greenland's new security deal with the US presents an opportunity to unlock American spending on the Arctic island, potentially boosting an economy still heavily dependent on subsidies and fish.
The accord signed in New York on Tuesday includes an agreement on two new US bases and states that contracts by the US should go to local businesses "to the maximum extent possible." That's raising hopes that spending on infrastructure and other activities could generate business for local companies and help establish defense as a new industry.
"We want it as a pillar of the economy," said Christian Keldsen, chief executive officer of the Greenland Business Association. "The beauty of defense activity is that there's an exchange: it's money coming into our society from the Danish or US government, while we provide something in return."
An additional benefit is that if local companies get contracts, "then we're creating Greenlandic jobs and building Greenlandic skills," Keldsen said.
The potential windfall comes as Greenland confronts a much bigger economic challenge. With gross domestic product of just $3.3 billion, the territory relies heavily on fishing and almost a billion dollars a year in subsidies from Denmark. Denmark's annual block grant alone accounts for roughly half of government revenue and a fifth of GDP.
That dependence has long complicated ambitions for greater economic independence on the island that's a semi-autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. In a report earlier this month, Greenland's Economic Council warned that an aging population, shrinking workforce and narrow economic base will put increasing pressure on the economy.
"What could make Greenland economically self-sustaining remains very unclear and is heavily influenced by everything happening geopolitically," said Torben M. Andersen, an economics professor who chairs the council. "There is still a way to go."
For now, the economy is picking up. After three years of growth below 1%, the council expects output to expand 1.3% in 2026 and 1.5% next year, helped by higher cod prices and catches that have offset declines in shrimp and Greenland halibut volumes. Cod catches have roughly doubled over the past five years, helping push seafood exports toward record levels.
But the rebound also illustrates Greenland's economic risks. Fish and shellfish account for more than 90% of total exports, according to Statistics Greenland, leaving the economy heavily exposed to swings in prices and fish stocks.
"Our economy becomes more vulnerable if we don't diversify it," Keldsen said. "It really hurts when you're standing on just one leg."
Efforts to branch out into tourism and mining — long seen as potential routes to greater economic independence — also face significant constraints. Tourism, which accounts for about 5% of GDP, has grown rapidly in recent years, pushing hotels and air travel to maximum capacity during the peak summer season. Further expansion will require more infrastructure and a longer tourist season.
Mining has an even longer road ahead. Greenland's vast but tricky-to-exploit mineral resources have become central to the geopolitical competition surrounding the island, yet years of exploration have translated into little commercial activity. Only two mines are currently operating, and several projects with permits have been unable to secure financing. The council says foreign investment is a prerequisite for broader development of the industry.
"It's just extremely difficult to get commercial investors to bite," Søren Bjerregaard, head of securities, balance of payments and financial statistics at Denmark's central bank, said at a recent presentation o
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Bill Gates Warns AI Powerful Enough to Lead to ‘a Billion Deaths’
item.author: Micah Barkley
item.description:
Bill Gates Warns AI Powerful Enough to Lead to ‘a Billion Deaths’
2026-09-28
Por Micah Barkley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/bill-gates-warns-ai-powerful-150039056.html
(Bloomberg) -- Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence is a "powerful enough" tool to kill off a substantial portion of humanity, joining a growing chorus of tech leaders and employees calling attention to AI's existential risks.
Most Read from Bloomberg
"AI is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths," Gates said in an excerpt of an interview with NBC's Meet the Press, set to air this weekend. "There's never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools."
Silicon Valley has escalated warnings about the potential for catastrophic harms from AI as the technology rapidly improves. Jacob Coxon, a rank-and-file staffer at Anthropic PBC, quit his job earlier this month and accused both his former employers — Anthropic and OpenAI — of "gambling with our lives" by "racing toward super-intelligent AI." Another Anthropic employee said he believes there is a greater-than-10% chance that AI eliminates all humans in the next decade.
Those remarks have led to mainstream attention for a long-running — and divisive — conversation within the field, prompting public calls for the industry to do more to safeguard its technology. Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei has since urged a slowdown in AI development, a proposal that was quickly supported by peers like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
In the interview, Gates said self-regulation is not enough. "You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like," he said. "And that has to be a required thing."
Gates previously argued in an August essay that bad actors could use increasingly powerful AI tools for cyberattacks, fraud, disinformation and other forms of large-scale harm against hospitals, financial institutions, power grids and government systems.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: New financing rules are about to make buying or selling a condo even more complicated
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
New financing rules are about to make buying or selling a condo even more complicated
2026-09-28
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/new-financing-rules-are-about-to-make-buying-or-selling-a-condo-even-more-complicated-150040903.html
It hasn't been an easy time to sell a condo, and new financing rules taking effect between now and early 2027 might make it even more complex.
Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the mortgage giants that support about 70% of the mortgage market, are tightening their standards for acceptable condo financing. "Limited reviews" that allowed many highly qualified buyers to receive mortgages after a cursory look at the financial and structural health of a condo building were eliminated last month, in favor of closer reviews for all but the smallest buildings. And starting in January, Fannie and Freddie will require condo associations to allocate at least 15% of their assessment income toward their reserves, up from 10% today.
The financing changes are part of an ongoing effort to improve condo safety after the deadly collapse of an aging building in Surfside, Fla., in 2021. But they're also a new roadblock in a market that's already seen slumping prices, growing supply, and increased buyer skepticism toward special assessments and monthly fees.
"A well-run, established HOA with solid reserves, acceptable finances, no major items like maintenance or litigation…should still be fine," said Michael Belfor, a mortgage banker and branch manager at American Pacific Mortgage in California. "But it absolutely does create more places for it to fail."
Read more: How to decide between a condo and a house
Market struggles
Condos have historically lagged the single-family home market, with prices quicker to drop and slower to rise due to their smaller buyer base. The divide has only deepened in recent years as housing affordability has deteriorated and buyers have begun to balk at association fees that can add hundreds or thousands of dollars a month to a mortgage payment.
To make matters worse, many condo associations have had to aggressively hike monthly fees or levy hefty special assessments to get in compliance with state regulations governing deferred maintenance and reserve funding.
The result? Nationally, condo prices have fallen 2% from peak prices a few years earlier, according to Zillow data. And in some parts of the country, especially Florida, the drop has been far steeper. Prices in Punta Gorda, Fla., have dropped 35% from their September 2022 peak, while Tampa has seen a 24% decline. Elsewhere, the median condo in Austin, Texas, is down 28%, while prices in Denver and Raleigh have fallen more than 16%.
Buyer demand remains weak. Condo sales were down 2.7% in August compared to a year earlier, according to National Association of Realtors data. Single-family home sales saw a smaller 1.1% drop. Nationwide, months of condo supply — a real estate industry measure of how long it would take to sell off all inventory at the current sales pace — sits at a buyer-friendly 6.6 months, while single-family homes are at a more balanced 4.7 months.

item.title: 'Out of nowhere came Muse': Wall Street weighs in on Meta's AI catch-up moment
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
'Out of nowhere came Muse': Wall Street weighs in on Meta's AI catch-up moment
2026-09-28
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/out-of-nowhere-came-muse-wall-street-weighs-in-on-metas-ai-catch-up-moment-131134524.html
Meta Platforms (META) just had a mic-drop moment.
The release of its AI agent Muse is giving investors a glimpse of how AI could be monetized with consumers.
"This new Muse agentic platform is taking over the internet," Futurum CEO Daniel Newman told Yahoo Finance.
Meta's Muse has quickly climbed the app charts, racking up millions of downloads in its first two weeks. Shares of the social media giant jumped roughly 13% past week and are on pace for their best month since July 2013.
The rally is notable given the stock's various drawdowns earlier this year.
"If you were paying attention, there were signs that there were good things ahead for Meta," added Newman.
But those signals were hard to see amid growing concerns over ballooning AI capital expenditures, claims of social media addiction, and the overhang from years of heavy Reality Labs losses.
Talk of AI risks and a potential development slowdown has also cast a shadow over the industry in recent weeks
The AI conversation has focused heavily on semiconductor giants riding the agentic AI wave, as well as enterprise adoption as companies spend heavily to boost productivity.
Other names in the space, such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google's Gemini, had garnered most of the attention this year.
"Then out of nowhere came Muse," Newman said.
Wall Street points to Meta's reset of its AI strategy last year, including the formation of its Super Intelligence Labs and a shift toward proprietary AI models, launching its closed Muse Spark model this year
"That team has been on fire over the past year," Justin Patterson, KeyBanc managing director, told Yahoo Finance on Thursday.
Analysts are especially bullish on Muse's consumer focus, an audience notoriously hard to monetize. Unlike Meta's core social platforms, which are paid for by advertising, Muse has no ads. Instead, the company plans to make money by taking a small cut on transactions made via the agent.
"We now have a consumer-facing AI product, which frankly, many companies have struggled with," said Patterson. "So Meta's gone from being viewed as a laggard in the past couple of months, to being viewed as a leader once again."
Wall Street is watching the Muse ecosystem get built out, with expectations that revenue will increase. More downloads and connectors will translate into more revenue and return on investment.
The stock currently has 73 Buys, 6 Holds, and 0 Sells. Dozens of analysts have raised their price targets on the stock over the past week, and the consensus now sits at $787.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: The deeper reason behind the relentless rise in bond yields
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The deeper reason behind the relentless rise in bond yields
2026-09-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-deeper-reason-behind-the-relentless-rise-in-bond-yields-120000422.html
Over the past few days, you have probably been hit over the head with stories about rising bond yields.
I hate to admit it, but I even churned out a host of stories on yields this week. Love me a good headline!
The rise in yields is one of the most important things happening in markets right now. Actually, this started in the summer, but you know what I mean.
"I would say [it's] not a crisis but an eye-opener, and it's something I think you've got to think about," BlackRock chief investment officer of global fixed income Rick Rieder said on Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed.
Rieder was among the finalists for the Fed chair role that ended up going to Kevin Warsh.
But I don't want you to lose focus on the "why" behind the move. It's not because of some warning on the nation's debt from some third-rate investing pundit. That's not the reason at all.
The reason is that the economy is weakening under the tightening grip of inflation. And this is going down just as the Federal Reserve makes it costlier for businesses and you, the consumer, to borrow money.
Here are a few red flags I have picked up on this week that no one is talking about, other than me.
- Execs at payroll services company Paychex (PAYX) said this week that we are in a low-hire, low-fire environment. Hardly a bullish economic endorsement.
- Lucky Charms maker General Mills (GIS) warned about more quarters of pressured margins at the hands of a big pickup in inflation in things like wheat, diesel, and packaging. I think this sheds light on what the Fed hawks like New York Fed president John Williams are telling us about rate hikes.
- Cracker Barrel (CBRL) called out a 6.1% traffic drop in its most recent quarter. Darden (DRI) said sales at its Olive Garden chain grew just 1.1% in the quarter. The read: Much higher gas prices are swallowing up the disposable income of many households.
It's always important to know the "why" when it comes to markets — and sadly, the "why" isn't great in the case of yields.

item.title: Goldman Sachs just gave AI stock fans a cold, hard reality check
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Goldman Sachs just gave AI stock fans a cold, hard reality check
2026-09-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/goldman-sachs-just-gave-ai-stock-fans-a-cold-hard-reality-check-121638833.html
It will take years for AI investments by major tech companies to pay off. But before that happens, companies have to break even — and that will also take years.
Goldman Sachs strategist Ryan Hammond crunched some numbers and thinks hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN), Oracle (ORCL), and Microsoft (MSFT) need to generate about $300 billion in AI revenue in the "next few years" to break even on their investments.
The hyperscalers have a ways to go before reaching that number, according to Hammond.
Hyperscaler cloud revenues have accelerated sharply this year, annualizing at about $70 billion above the pre-AI trend in the second quarter of 2026. Announced backlogs for the group exceed $1.5 trillion.
"We estimate that AI users would need to spend roughly $1 trillion annually on AI applications in order for the hyperscalers to generate solid returns on investment and the application layer to generate strong profit margins on their compute expenses," Hammond wrote.
The stakes are high for investors, who have plowed back into hyperscaler stocks in recent weeks amid AI optimism.
The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) — which tracks the performance of top AI hyperscalers — is up 8% inside of a month compared to a modest gain for the S&P 500 (^GSPC).

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) — which tracks the performance of top AI hyperscalers — is up 8% inside of a month compared to a modest gain for the S&P 500 (^GSPC).

item.title: Billionaire Charlie Munger, 99, Said His Life Worked Better Treating Elon Musk Like He Didn’t ‘Exist’ — ‘I Never Bet Against Him, But I Never Bet With Him’
item.author: Jeannine Mancini
item.description:
Billionaire Charlie Munger, 99, Said His Life Worked Better Treating Elon Musk Like He Didn’t ‘Exist’ — ‘I Never Bet Against Him, But I Never Bet With Him’
2026-09-26
Por Jeannine Mancini
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/billionaire-charlie-munger-99-said-173015712.html
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
The late longtime Berkshire Hathaway Vice Chair Charlie Munger didn't need to dislike a business to stay away from it. Sometimes, he simply decided it belonged in the "too hard" pile.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk was a perfect example. Munger respected what Musk had accomplished, but he wasn't interested in taking the same risks that helped get him there.
The two had a history that went back to Tesla's early days.
"I was at a lunch with Munger in 2009 where he told the whole table all the ways Tesla would fail," Musk wrote on X in 2022. "Made me quite sad, but I told him I agreed with all those reasons and that we would probably die, but it was worth trying anyway."
Don't Miss:
Tesla obviously didn't die. In fact, its success eventually forced Munger to acknowledge that Musk had accomplished something extraordinary.
At Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting in 2023, Munger said there hadn't been a successful new American auto company in a long time and called Tesla's achievement a "minor miracle." He also acknowledged that Musk had accomplished important things by pursuing problems that seemed almost impossible to solve.
That history made Munger's final interview even more interesting.
The CNBC interview was taped just two weeks before his death at 99. It was originally intended to air around what would have been his 100th birthday, but Munger died on Nov. 28, 2023.
When host Becky Quick brought up Musk, Munger made clear that he still wasn't convinced the Tesla CEO's fortune was as secure as it appeared.
"I don't regard Elon Musk as truly that rich because I don't think it's sure that everything he's working on can work," Munger said. "I think he can get his a** handed to him on autos. I would not invest in Elon Musk's autos myself."
Munger Respected Musk Without Wanting His Risk
Quick then pointed out that Munger had clearly been impressed by what Musk had built.
"Yes, well, who cannot?" he replied.
The answer wasn't a dismissal of Musk's accomplishments. Instead, Munger used the opening to explain what he believed was behind them.
"Again, that's another lesson," Munger said. "What is the lesson of Elon Musk? Somebody who has a perfectly ridiculous amount of money almost always has an element of luck in him.".
Trending: 'The Walking Dead' And 'Invincible' Are Two Of Skybound's Biggest Hits. What Else Is In Its Portfolio?
He then returned to Musk's willingness to keep doubling down on his biggest bets.
"He's been quite lucky in what he's picked to double down, double down, double down — and then he's used leverage so much that he has doubled down right to the edge of extinction maybe two or three times," Munger said.
That kind of risk-taking was precisely what Munger preferred to avoid.
"How many people can go to the edge of extinction without stepping into it?" he asked. "Well, he's done it three times. Maybe he's got six more in him — I don't know."
Then came the clearest explanation of where Musk fit into Munger's investment framework.
"I put Elon Musk in a too-hard pile," he said. "I never bet against him, but I never bet with him."
Munger finished with a line that captured just how completely he preferred to keep that kind of risk outside his own portfolio.
"As far as I'm concerned, he doesn't exist. My life works better if I treat the world as though he didn't exist," he said.
Compounding Was Munger's Other Big Bet
Munger's own approach to wealth building was almost the mirror image of Musk's willingness to repeatedly make enormous bets.

item.title: Over 30 CEOs scored an invite to the US-China state dinner — and these 4 got a spot at the head table
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Over 30 CEOs scored an invite to the US-China state dinner — and these 4 got a spot at the head table
2026-09-26
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/over-30-ceos-scored-an-invite-to-the-us-china-state-dinner--and-these-4-got-a-spot-at-the-head-table-134400923.html
President Trump touted Thursday's long-awaited state dinner at the White House as a tough ticket, and while the Chinese business delegation was notably absent, the glittering event featured a wide array of US CEOs.
The official invite list included more than 30 present or former US CEOs, largely from the technology sector, as well as from banking, carmakers, and pharmaceuticals.
Perhaps most striking were the four CEOs whom Trump's team chose to sit at the head table with the two heads of state.
Elon Musk of Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) was seated next to Melania Trump, while Jensen Huang of Nvidia (NVDA), former Apple (AAPL) CEO Tim Cook, as well as Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) filled out the head table.
In his remarks before the crowd, Trump said the US and Chinese relationship has been built on a "foundation of commerce and mutual respect between our countries, and together we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations."
The dinner menu, according to the White House, featured three courses to showcase "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence," including a wild mushroom fricassée, sesame-crusted sea bass, and honey ice cream.
The central table at a State Dinner at the WHite House featured US President Donald Trump, US First Lady Melania Trump, Elon Musk, Lisa Su, Daniel Lin (Lisa Su's husband), Jensen Huang Lori Huang, Tim Cook, Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan, and Chinese President Xi Jinping (speaking). (AP Photo/Alex Brandon) ·AP Photo/Alex Brandon
The guest list was notable for the outsized presence of tech CEOs and leaders in artificial intelligence. Huang, in particular, has spoken out in recent days against government regulations on the sector, a position Trump has often echoed.
One of the attendees, Satya Nadella of Microsoft, spoke to Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa earlier this week and offered optimism about the overall US-China relationship, saying of AI, "I think both sides will care about the same set of things at the end of the day, which is they want to be able to have this technology actually help their citizens get value." He said safety will be an important element for both sides as norms are set.
The dinner — like many previous Trump events — mixed CEOs among administration officials, Republican party leaders, Fox News hosts, and Supreme Court justices.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio was at a nearby table, seated next to Citigroup (C) CEO Jane Fraser. Former Amazon (AMZN) CEO Jeff Bezos was seated next to Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, according to a photo.
OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) CEO Sam Altman was also close at hand, along with White House Deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino (an aide who has been at Trump's side since the 1990s) and Meta (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
Story Continues
Other business world names included Kelly Ortberg of Boeing (BA), Larry Fink of BlackRock (BLK), Sergey Brin of Google (GOOG), Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Mary Barra of General Motors (GM), Darren Woods of ExxonMobil (XOM), David Ellison of Paramount Skydance (PSKY), and Albert Bourla of Pfizer (PFE).
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman talks with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg as President Donald Trump hosts a State Dinner for China's President Xi Jinping in the East Room of the White House. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon) ·AP Photo/Alex Brandon
Here's the full list of invited guests provided by the White House
President Donald J. Trump
First Lady Melania Trump
President Xi Jinping
Madame Peng Liyuan
Vice President JD Vance
Second Lady Usha Vance
Secretary of State Marco Rubio
Jeanette Rubio, spouse of the Secretary of State
Chief of staff Susie
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Costco is getting squeezed by the AI boom
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Costco is getting squeezed by the AI boom
2026-09-26
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/costco-is-getting-squeezed-by-the-ai-boom-133927696.html
Even mighty Costco (COST), with all its buying power over suppliers, can't escape the inflationary impact of America's AI boom, which is pushing up prices for things like laptop computers and smartphones.
"So what we're seeing overall currently, if I add together the sort of cumulative impact in all of our merchandising categories, we feel like inflation currently is running in the low single digits, and it's relatively stable overall from what we've seen in prior quarters," Costco CFO Gary Millerchip said on the company's earnings call late Thursday.
"The area where we did see some increase in the current quarter was in non-foods," Millerchip continued. "That was really, I wouldn't say it was isolated, but the vast majority of it was in memory costs on consumer electronics and the items that you would expect to be related to oil."
The pressured margins in consumer electronics weighed on Costco's overall margins: Gross profit margins fell to 11.01% in the fiscal fourth quarter from 11.12% a year ago.
Watch Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed daily at 9:30 a.m. ET
There's no end in sight for Costco on the chip inflation front.
The memory chip market has tightened considerably as demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) used in AI servers continues to outpace supply.
Companies such as SK Hynix (SKHY), Samsung Electronics (005930.KS), and Micron (MU) have largely sold out their premium AI memory capacity through much of 2026 as customers, including Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta (META), race to build AI infrastructure.
The shortage has pushed memory prices sharply higher and given suppliers greater pricing power after several years of weak industry conditions.
Experts expect memory supply to remain constrained into 2027, creating a favorable backdrop for the industry's largest producers, such as Micron and Sandisk (SNDK).
For its part, Costco still managed to deliver a solid quarter as cost-conscious consumers flocked to its warehouse amid the surge in gas prices.
Total sales rose 11.1% from the prior year to $95.72 billion. Total comparable store sales surged 9.4%. Online sales rose 19.5%.
"Membership growth is moderating, yet the company's ability to drive deeper engagement, leverage its fuel advantage, grow digital penetration, and reinforce its value leadership leaves it exceptionally well positioned if consumers remain focused on stretching their dollars further. In our view, Costco remains one of retail's highest quality long-term compounders," Jefferies analyst Corey Tarlowe said.
