Companies such as SK Hynix (SKHY), Samsung Electronics (005930.KS), and Micron (MU) have largely sold out their premium AI memory capacity through much of 2026 as customers, including Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta (META), race to build AI infrastructure.
The shortage has pushed memory prices sharply higher and given suppliers greater pricing power after several years of weak industry conditions.
Experts expect memory supply to remain constrained into 2027, creating a favorable backdrop for the industry's largest producers, such as Micron and Sandisk (SNDK).
For its part, Costco still managed to deliver a solid quarter as cost-conscious consumers flocked to its warehouse amid the surge in gas prices.
Total sales rose 11.1% from the prior year to $95.72 billion. Total comparable store sales surged 9.4%. Online sales rose 19.5%.
"Membership growth is moderating, yet the company's ability to drive deeper engagement, leverage its fuel advantage, grow digital penetration, and reinforce its value leadership leaves it exceptionally well positioned if consumers remain focused on stretching their dollars further. In our view, Costco remains one of retail's highest quality long-term compounders," Jefferies analyst Corey Tarlowe said.

item.title: Meta has an AI solution to its misunderstood trust problem
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Meta has an AI solution to its misunderstood trust problem
2026-09-26
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/meta-has-an-ai-solution-to-its-misunderstood-trust-problem-100000057.html
Meta's Muse has the "it" factor. After a flashy debut, it quickly won over early adopters and analysts for being the first capable AI agent for normies.
But a trickier question is whether Zuckerberg and company have the trust factor.
Of all the tech CEOs, perhaps none have as much trust and safety baggage as Zuckerberg. His rise to tech emperor was immortalized in the movie "The Social Network," which you could even say was about trust.
But will enough people feel assured enough in Meta to plug Muse into their wallets, calendars, inboxes, and shopping carts?
That's why, as Justin Patterson, KeyBanc managing director, told Yahoo Finance, "Meta is having its moment." After the Muse announcement, Patterson was among the analysts to raise his price target on Meta. He sees $900. Shares are up almost 13% over the past week.
Maybe saying users won't trust Muse to be their AI agent is denying how much people already depend on the Meta umbrella for their digital lives. Or maybe, as Meta sees it, people will take Muse's privacy safeguards seriously. Zuckerberg has emphasized that his teams designed state-of-the-art privacy and security into Muse's systems from the beginning.

item.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on AI: ‘Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us’
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on AI: ‘Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us’
2026-09-26
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/microsoft-ceo-satya-nadella-on-ai-trust-is-going-to-be-the-biggest-issue-for-us-163733897.html
Microsoft (MSFT) on Friday unveiled a revamped version of its Copilot software, combining its chat, coding, and agentic capabilities into a single package, which it calls Autopilot.
The platform is designed to serve as a kind of one-stop shop for your work needs, such as preparing a pitch document or putting together a spreadsheet, then having AI reason over the data to provide users with insights they may not see.
But to ensure it wins over customers, CEO Satya Nadella said, Microsoft will need to win users' trust.
"Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us," Nadella told Deirdre Bosa.
"Can I really trust [AI] with all of my credentials when it does autonomous activity? How do I make sure that this is something that I can feel that I'm in control of? And in the enterprise, this is everything," he said.
The new Copilot also offers two billing options: standard per-user plans for general AI work and a pay-as-you-go option for long-tail, multistep agentic work.
Nadella said the dual offerings will prove especially beneficial to users as AI model makers and providers gradually reduce customer subsidies.
"The way I think about our subscriptions [is] it's ultimately going to deliver more value every day of the week as models improve. And then on top of that, we have usage-based functionality that any user at any time can use with no limits," the CEO explained.
"And so that combination gives us, I think, the right business model to be able to both deliver broad access, deliver the [return on investment] that's expected, and most importantly, continuously be aligned with where customers will see value," he said.
Microsoft said Copilot will automatically route user prompts to the best available model from OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) and Anthropic (ANTH.PVT), though you'll also be able to manually choose models. The company said it will add additional options from other model makers in the future.
The Windows maker said that the per-seat option will have token limits that most people will never hit.
Those who need additional capabilities, however, can opt for usage-based billing.

item.title: Consumer sentiment falls to 4-month low as concerns over inflation mount
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Consumer sentiment falls to 4-month low as concerns over inflation mount
2026-09-26
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/consumer-sentiment-falls-to-4-month-low-as-concerns-over-inflation-mount-153320190.html
Consumer sentiment fell in September as higher grocery and gas prices weighed on Americans' views of the economy, according to a survey from the University of Michigan.
Overall consumer sentiment fell to 48.1 in September, down from August's 51.7, as consumers' expectations for their personal finances weakened by about 10%. The reading was slightly above the Street's expectation of 47.5.
"The short-run outlook for business conditions plunged amid renewed worries that elevated fuel prices and re-escalating trade disputes could pass through to the economy as a whole," Joanne Hsu, the survey's director, said in the release.
Read more: What is consumer confidence, and why does it matter?
Following talks that had collapsed between the US and Canada in late August, President Trump placed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods. This week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the US and China would extend their current trade truce, with talks set to continue in early 2027.
Hsu added that consumers' outlook for the economy has weakened across the political spectrum since the start of the year.
As inflation remained elevated in August and the war with Iran continues, Americans' outlook for inflation in the year ahead jumped to 4.6% in September from 4% in August, marking the highest reading since June.
It's also far higher than inflation expectations of 3.4% seen in February and all readings in 2024.
Gas prices have increased by more than $1.50 on average since the beginning of the war, according to AAA, and are now creeping toward $5 per gallon nationwide. In California, average prices are above $6 per gallon.
Long-term inflation expectations increased to 3.4% in September, ending three consecutive months at 3.3%. In recent months, they have consistently remained above the 2.8%-3.2% range seen in 2024.
Brooke DiPalma is a reporter for Yahoo Finance. Follow her on X at @BrookeDiPalma or email her at bdipalma@yahoofinance.com.

item.title: Trump Advisers Analyzing Impact of Short-Term Diesel Export Ban
item.author: Jennifer A Dlouhy; Erik Wasson
item.description:
Trump Advisers Analyzing Impact of Short-Term Diesel Export Ban
2026-09-26
Por Jennifer A Dlouhy; Erik Wasson
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/trump-advisers-analyzing-impact-short-211304949.html
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump's economic advisers are analyzing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports, underscoring the seriousness of the administration's consideration of the idea.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Senator John Hoeven, a Republican from North Dakota, said the study being conducted by National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer aims to inform the administration's decision-making on possible export curbs.
"The idea is that you get Bessent and Greer and Hassett to do that analysis and if, on a short-term basis — and we are in harvest season right now — it would show that it would help, then it is something we should consider doing," Hoeven said.
Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit foreign sales of US diesel, as conflicts in Russia and the Middle East take supplies offline and spike prices for the fuel right at the peak of the fall harvest season in the US.
Diesel is essential for powering farm equipment and is a critical fuel for modern shipping, propelling freight trains, long-haul trucks and delivery vans. And its retail cost — which hit a new high this week and averaged $6.51 per gallon on Wednesday — is adding to voter anxieties about the cost of living ahead of November's midterm elections.
A timeline for the government's economic analysis was not immediately available. But the study, described by people familiar with the matter, is expected to forecast a mix of potential consequences — including both lower and higher prices — that could be used by administration officials either to justify or ward off a ban.
The study shouldn't be viewed as an indication the administration is leaning one way or the other, one of the people said. Instead, it's a standard analysis, like others routinely used by the White House to examine potential economic policies, the person said.
Energy experts have said export curbs could yield temporary price discounts on diesel initially, with refiners blocked from selling to foreign buyers. However, those short-term price reductions would likely fade swiftly — and be replaced with even higher costs — as rising US fuel inventories prompt oil producers and refiners to cut output.

item.title: This Meta stock stat doesn't make sense after the Muse mic drop
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
This Meta stock stat doesn't make sense after the Muse mic drop
2026-09-26
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/this-meta-stock-stat-doesnt-make-sense-after-the-muse-mic-drop-160000647.html
For a company having a major refounding moment this week, Meta's (META) price-to-earnings ratio still looks stuck in the past.
Meta's stock is trading on a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 22 times, below its long-term average of 23.1 times.
The likely reason for the disconnect between Meta's P/E and the bullish week the company's having is that the Street is dragging its feet on raising its 2027 earnings estimates as the company reinvests aggressively in AI infrastructure.
Yahoo Finance data shows next year's earnings estimates on Meta have increased only slightly over the past seven days. Meanwhile, 2027 EPS estimates currently remain well below those seen 90 days ago.
But the EPS trend is poised to change, and investors are betting on that today — Meta stock has surged 14% in the past five days.
Meta's Steve Jobs-like surprise at Meta Connect late Wednesday came in the form of the Muse Charm. It's a standalone pocket device built exclusively for voice interaction with the company's new Muse agent, currently one of the most-downloaded apps.
Zuckerberg also showcased a major shift toward "Personal Superintelligence" by unveiling a hardware-meets-AI moment in the Meta VR Glasses.
Weighing just 100 grams — roughly one-fifth the weight of Meta's Quest 3 — the $1,299 spatial computing glasses feature 5K micro-OLED displays, tethered puck processing, and native eye and hand tracking.
On the smart eyewear front, Meta debuted the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses, starting at an entry-level $249. Joining them are the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, designed purely for open-ear listening and AI voice interaction.
Meanwhile, Meta's Muse has amassed more than 3.4 million downloads since its Sept. 8 launch, per new Sensor Tower data obtained by Yahoo Finance.
Muse accumulated 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks, while competitor AI chatbots, including OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) ChatGPT, SpaceXAI's (SPCX) Grok, and Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude, received 3.7 million, 400,000, and 300,000 global downloads, respectively, during the same period (14 days post-launch).
"We emerge from Meta Connect incrementally positive on shares of Meta as its AI product strategy comes into view across Muse, its Models, and newer devices," Citi analyst Ronald Josey said. "Key here, Muse is emerging as the centerpiece of Meta's AI product strategy as voice, additional distribution points (Meta Glasses), and services/capabilities are integrated across shopping, travel, and productivity verticals, enabling Muse to connect consumer intent with execution potentially unlocking incremental monetization opportunities, in our view."

"We emerge from Meta Connect incrementally positive on shares of Meta as its AI product strategy comes into view across Muse, its Models, and newer devices," Citi analyst Ronald Josey said. "Key here, Muse is emerging as the centerpiece of Meta's AI product strategy as voice, additional distribution points (Meta Glasses), and services/capabilities are integrated across shopping, travel, and productivity verticals, enabling Muse to connect consumer intent with execution potentially unlocking incremental monetization opportunities, in our view."

2026-09-26

For a company having a major refounding moment this week, Meta's (META) price-to-earnings ratio still looks stuck in the past.
Meta's stock is trading on a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 22 times, below its long-term average of 23.1 times.
The likely reason for the disconnect between Meta's P/E and the bullish week the company's having is that the Street is dragging its feet on raising its 2027 earnings estimates as the company reinvests aggressively in AI infrastructure.
Yahoo Finance data shows next year's earnings estimates on Meta have increased only slightly over the past seven days. Meanwhile, 2027 EPS estimates currently remain well below those seen 90 days ago.
But the EPS trend is poised to change, and investors are betting on that today — Meta stock has surged 14% in the past five days.
Meta's Steve Jobs-like surprise at Meta Connect late Wednesday came in the form of the Muse Charm. It's a standalone pocket device built exclusively for voice interaction with the company's new Muse agent, currently one of the most-downloaded apps.
Zuckerberg also showcased a major shift toward "Personal Superintelligence" by unveiling a hardware-meets-AI moment in the Meta VR Glasses.
Weighing just 100 grams — roughly one-fifth the weight of Meta's Quest 3 — the $1,299 spatial computing glasses feature 5K micro-OLED displays, tethered puck processing, and native eye and hand tracking.

item.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su is having a September to remember
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AMD CEO Lisa Su is having a September to remember
2026-09-26
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/amd-ceo-lisa-su-is-having-a-september-to-remember-135902902.html
AMD (AMD) CEO Lisa Su is getting her due and becoming one of the most well-respected CEOs in tech after years of flying under the radar.
No doubt she is having a September to remember.
Su was photographed sitting with her husband, Daniel Lin, at President Trump's table during the state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. She was seated next to Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk.
What's more, she was only two seats away from President Trump. Chip rival CEO Jensen Huang of Nvidia (NVDA) was seated across from Trump with his wife, Lori.
On Wednesday, Su got some prime face time with first lady Melania Trump at the New York Stock Exchange, where they rang the opening bell and then had a fireside chat.
But this was all just icing on the cake to a monumental week for Su and her investor base.
AMD's market cap crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time on Monday, with shares surging 9.9% amid a broader tech-stock rally. The company's market cap is likely to close above that level this week.
The moment made Su the first inductee into the Sozzi Unleashed "Wall of Titans" (detailed in the video above).
AMD stock is up an impressive 193% year to date, easily surpassing the 22% gain for Nvidia.
The chipmaker has had win after win this year, fueling its stock price.
AMD beat Wall Street expectations across the board for the second quarter earlier this month, posting record non-GAAP earnings per share of $1.66 versus consensus estimates of $1.61. Total revenue surged 50% year over year to a record $11.5 billion, clearing analyst projections of approximately $11.34 billion.
The strong top- and bottom-line performance was fueled by the company's data center segment. Revenue more than doubled year over year to $6.7 billion behind robust demand for EPYC server CPUs and Instinct AI accelerators.
AMD projected second-half 2026 server CPU revenue to grow 80% year over year and 70% in 2027. It expects data center revenues to more than double in 2027, with AI graphics processing units (GPUs) growing well over 100%.
AMD also unveiled its next-generation AI chips, headlined by the Instinct MI450 Series GPUs and the 6th Gen EPYC Venice CPUs. The new chips are designed to power AMD's new Helios rack-scale AI systems, which combine GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software into an integrated platform for training and running large AI models.
The product announcement came alongside two important new deals.
AMD said Microsoft (MSFT) will deploy Helios across Azure AI services beginning in the second half of 2026.

item.title: Microsoft CEO: We 'have to earn that permission’ to build data centers from communities
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Microsoft CEO: We 'have to earn that permission’ to build data centers from communities
2026-09-26
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/microsoft-ceo-we-have-to-earn-that-permission-to-build-data-centers-from-communities-172505836.html
The AI data center build-out has turned Nvidia (NVDA) into a $5 trillion company, is helping to power Intel's (INTC) turnaround efforts, and made memory chip makers some of the hottest companies on Earth.
But a growing number of Americans see the boom as a burden being forced upon them that is gobbling up land, power, and water. Coupled with non-disclosure agreements that some companies require towns to sign, the situation has become volatile.
An increasing number of states have introduced legislation halting or banning the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a state-wide, one-year moratorium. Texas has similarly blocked new data center projects until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes an audit to assess the facilities' impact on Texas's power grid and water resources.to halt or ban the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a statewide
To address the matter, Microsoft (MSFT) is taking a more open approach to its data center plans. In March, the company announced it was ending the use of non-disclosure agreements and terminating existing ones.
"At the end of the day, I think we have to get permission from the communities," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told Deirdre Bosa. "If you are going to be building a data center, consuming power, using water, at the end of the day, we have to earn that permission."
The move is part of what Microsoft calls its Community-First AI Infrastructure Plan. Unveiled in January, the effort includes the software giant paying to ensure electricity rates in data-center areas don't rise, minimizing and replenishing more water than the company uses, hiring local workers, not asking communities to reduce taxes on data centers, and investing in AI training.
"We have a set of commitments, right? I don't think of anything that we do as building a data center and getting out. No. It's about being able to be welcomed in the community on an ongoing basis," Nadella explained.
The CEO pointed to Microsoft's efforts in Quincy, Wash., as an example of how the company says it can move forward. Since Microsoft began constructing its first company-owned data center in 2006, Quincy's poverty rate has declined from 29.4% to 13.1% between 2012 and 2023.
Tax rates for residents have also declined, while the improved tax base has helped pay for a new hospital and other municipal facilities, according to Microsoft.
"They have a new hospital, they have a new school. They have a new city center. And over the years, we've also created a lot of employment opportunities. We have close to a thousand people there," Nadella said.

item.title: Fifteen years later, the Apple Cards origin story
item.author: Lex Friedman
item.description:
Fifteen years later, the Apple Cards origin story
2026-09-25
Por Lex Friedman
https://lexontech.org/fifteen-years-later-the-apple-cards-origin-story
In 2011, Apple released the Cards app. The app — which required iOS 5 — let you design custom letterpress cards, with your messages and photos printed upon them — which Apple would ship to your recipient on your behalf.
I recently learned the origin story of Cards, and that it was specifically a Steve Jobs product. It also wasn’t smooth sailing. But first, some backstory, and inserting myself into the narrative, because it’s my site and I can do what I want here.
I wrote about the app several times for Macworld. Apple complained first to me, and later to my editors, that I didn’t go deep on the fact that the cards Apple was offering were printed on 100 percent cotton paper. Apple thought my article should be updated to mention this. My editors and I disagreed.
I wasn’t the only person ever to get in trouble with Apple over Cards.
In 2019, someone wrote me this email:
I ran the print program for Apple’s production and fulfillment partner in those years. In my decade working with Apple and in fact my 30-year career, this project — code named Speed Racer and dreamed up by Steve Jobs himself — stands unsurpassed as a pinnacle of incompetence, project mismanagement and intercontinental mayhem. I hope to never top it.
It is probably best left dead, but if you felt like disinterring it, I’m a witness to the crime…
It took me seven years to reply. I don’t know why.
Although Apple launched cards in 2011, and it’s now 15 years later, this person — despite his confidence that any non-disclosure agreements have long since expired, his knowledge that the Cards app was sunset long ago, and the fact that the printing companies involved no longer really exist — still asked to remain anonymous, for fear of angering Apple.
I get it.
I’m going to call this person Mike.
The prints of darkness
In 2006, Mike was hired at a printing company that already had a relationship with Apple, handling printing for iPhoto, which let you order custom books, calendars, and cards. The company had won that business because it was also, at the time, handling Apple’s in-box production of documentation — quick start guides, instruction manuals, and the like. (Remember those?)
For several years, this company worked as the exclusive Apple partner for those print products, after Apple had grown frustrated with a prior photo printing partner.
Order volume was massive, Mike told me on a Zoom, especially between Thanksgiving and Christmas when card and calendar volume exploded. The printing company had to spin up several sister companies to handle the load. They printed internationally, too; Mike, as essentially the program manager, also stood up print operations in the Czech Republic and Japan.
In 2010, Apple added a new product to the iPhoto print lineup — codenamed Downieville. Apple wanted fine letterpress printing on very toothy cotton stock. Your photo would be digitally printed on these preprinted shells.
This, Mike told me, was an enormous technical challenge. The printing company had to work with a shop in upstate New York that had two dozen restored Heidelberg Letterpresses from the 1850s.
The Steve Jobs origin story
In 2011, Mike said, “Steve Jobs was on one of his famous walks after having had a dinner with someone,” and he said to his walking companions from Apple, Mike was later told: “Wouldn’t it be great if I could just right now on my iPhone send [the dinner companion] a thank you card?”
Apple decided to build an iPhone app just for creating and mailing cards. And the project moved fast, because it was a Steve-initiated one. As it turns out, the app was built and launched during the final year of Steve’s life.
The project kicked off in the beginning of 2011, and it didn’t reuse the card designs that were in iPhoto. These were new designs and letterpress templates and shells. And Apple
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Sin prompt ni ayuda, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de OpenAI hackeó el sistema de salud de Australia
item.author: Karla Pesantes
item.description:
Sin prompt ni ayuda, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de OpenAI hackeó el sistema de salud de Australia
2026-09-25
Por Karla Pesantes
https://www.primicias.ec/internacional/modelo-ia-openai-hackeo-sistema-salud-australia-133317/
Sin prompt ni ayuda, un modelo de inteligencia artificial de OpenAI hackeó el sistema de salud de Australia
Un modelo de OpenAI, empresa detrás del ChatGPT, eludió las medidas de seguridad durante su entrenamiento y hackeó un sitio web del gobierno australiano, afirmó el primer ministro Anthony Albanese.
El CEO de OpenAI, Sam Altman, cuando llegó a una reunión del Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU, Nueva York, el 24 de septiembre de 2026.
- Foto
Getty Images via AFP
Autor:
Redacción Primicias / AFP
Actualizada:
Compartir:
En otro caso más de la 'sublevación' o desobediencia de la IA, Australia reportó este 24 de septiembre que un modelo de inteligencia artificial de la empresa OpenAI hackeó un portal del sistema de salud del país.
Sin ayuda de un 'humano' ni la orden dada por un prompt, el modelo de IA accedió a un portal de estadísticas de salud en junio, reveló este miércoles el premier de Australia, Anthony Albanese.
Según Albanese, el sistema de IA "no aceptó un no por respuesta", y siguió con la vulneración del sistema de salud, al citar las restricciones que tiene la plataforma australiana, para invadir una sección que albergaba archivos privados.
Lo más grave es que OpenAI no alertó al gobierno australiano hasta septiembre, cuando envió un correo electrónico con los detalles del incidente a una dirección genérica que solo se revisa "una vez al día", según Australia.
Esta nueva infiltración de un modelo de IA se reporta luego que Sam Altman, CEO de OpenAI, y otros ejecutivos de la alta tecnología intervinieron el miércoles en una sesión especial del Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU sobre los riesgos de la IA.
La preocupación mundial por el poder de los modelos avanzados de IA va en aumento tras una serie de incidentes de piratería que involucraron "agentes" tanto de OpenAI como de su desarrollador rival, Anthropic.
Más de 100 organizaciones en todo el mundo, incluidas OpenAI y Anthropic, firmaron una carta abierta en la que llamaron a un esfuerzo global para "fortalecer las defensas" cibernéticas de las amenazas a la seguridad causadas por la IA.
Esto ocurrió después de que dos modelos de OpenAI se escaparan de un entorno de pruebas cerrado y se infiltraran en los sistemas internos de Hugging Face, un sitio que los desarrolladores de IA utilizan para almacenar y compartir código.
Australia reprende a OpenAI
"Hoy hablé con el director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, para expresar la enorme preocupación de Australia sobre este incidente", aseguró el primer ministro de Australia.
"También expresé mi decepción por el hecho de que la empresa tardó demasiado en informar al gobierno de lo ocurrido", agregó Albanese.
"No hubo ninguna notificación hasta el 10 de septiembre, y la notificación fue un correo electrónico enviado únicamente al buzón público".
Anthony Albanese, premier de Australia
La herramienta de IA accedió a archivos públicos y restringidos alojados en un antiguo sitio web de estadísticas de salud.
Albanese señaló que "no hay evidencia" de que se haya accedido a información personal y que otros servicios gubernamentales no se vieron comprometidos.
La filtración ocurrió en junio, cuando la empresa líder en inteligencia artificial OpenAI realizó ejercicios de entrenamiento para evaluar el desempeño de los modelos de IA.
Le pidió al modelo que rastreara internet en busca de datos que mostraran cuánto gastaba el gobierno australiano en medicamentos, explicó la ministra de Servicios Gubernamentales, Katy Gallagher, a periodistas.
OpenAI afirmó que no detectó la actividad no autorizada hasta agosto, cuando revisó lo que la herramienta de IA había estado haciendo.

item.title: De la Serie A al 'infierno' de Segunda en 281 días: los cuatro hitos que explican el virtual descenso de El Nacional
item.author: Pablo Campos
item.description:
De la Serie A al 'infierno' de Segunda en 281 días: los cuatro hitos que explican el virtual descenso de El Nacional
2026-09-25
Por Pablo Campos
https://www.primicias.ec/deportes/ligapro/nacional/crisis-hitos-descenso-segunda-categoria-criollos-deudas-dirigencias-133263/
De la Serie A al 'infierno' de Segunda en 281 días: los cuatro hitos que explican el virtual descenso de El Nacional
El Nacional pasó de la Serie A a estar prácticamente descendido a la Segunda Categoría en menos de un año. La profunda crisis se aceleró desde diciembre de 2025 debido a las malas decisiones.
El Nacional pasó, en menos de un año, de la Serie A a la Segunda División del fútbol ecuatoriano.
- Foto
Composición fotográfica PRIMICIAS
Compartir:
El Nacional pasó de la Serie A a estar virtualmente descendido a la Segunda Categoría en menos de un año. Transcurrieron exactamente 281 días (40 semanas, nueve meses y siete días) desde que el 'Bitri' perdió la categoría principal hasta quedar condenado al fútbol de Segunda.
El 10 de diciembre de 2025, el Tribunal de Apelaciones de la Federación Ecuatoriana de Fútbol (FEF) confirmó el descenso del 'Rojo'. Desde entonces, una serie de crisis de gobernanza, administrativas, económicas y deportivas desembocaron en la dolorosa debacle.
El desenlace llegó la noche del viernes 17 de septiembre de 2026, cuando el equipo perdió ante Deportivo Santo Domingo en el hexagonal de permanencia de la Serie B.
El 'Bitri' se quedó con 12 puntos y -19 de gol diferencia, una distancia insalvable ante Cumbayá, su rival directo, que suma 30 unidades y +24 de gol diferencia.
El viernes 25 de septiembre de 2026, ambos clubes se enfrentarán en el estadio La Cocha. Restan seis fechas (18 puntos en disputa), la misma distancia que separa a los 'puros criollos' de la salvación.
Una victoria del 'Rojo' solo servirá para alargar la agonía, pero parece imposible. El Nacional sólo ha ganado tres partidos de 26 que ha disputado en esta temporada.
El interventor del club militar, Juan Manuel Aguirre, le contó a PRIMICIAS que el déficit institucional alcanza los USD 12 millones, aunque la auditoría interna y los reclamos de acreedores siguen bajo revisión. Las deudas se acumularon durante los últimos siete años, pero la situación empeoró drásticamente entre 2025 y 2026.
¿Cómo se explica este año tormentoso? A continuación, los cuatro hitos fundamentales de la debacle:
1. El descenso a la Serie B y la renuncia de Marco Pazos
Diciembre de 2025 fue el mes clave. El día 10, el Tribunal de Apelaciones de la Federación Ecuatoriana de Fútbol restó nueve puntos al club por inconsistencias en la documentación de acuerdos de pago. El equipo pasó de 42 a 33 puntos en la tabla y descendió por gol diferencia.
Seis días después, el presidente Marco Pazos renunció junto con el primer vocal, Pablo Erazo. “Me quedé sin apoyo de los dueños del club. El Comando Conjunto no me respaldó; no podía quedarme”, justificó Pazos en radio La Red.
El 16 de diciembre asumió el mando el general Ricardo Cajas, comandante de la Fuerza Terrestre del Ejército. Cajas reconoció a PRIMICIAS que sus responsabilidades militares limitaban su tiempo para administrar una institución que ya registraba un déficit de USD 11 millones para finales de 2025.
Un día después de asumir, Cajas firmó un acuerdo de entendimiento con el grupo Naniecheandia SL SA (NEF) para liderar el salvataje. “El club estaba quebrado. Si no tomábamos esa decisión, nos íbamos a Segunda Categoría en ese mismo diciembre”, justificó el dirigente. Sin embargo, la alianza no entregó la solución esperada.
2. La alianza con NEF duró cuatro meses y no 15 años
Cajas y Xiomara Contreras, CEO de Naniecheandia SL SA, suscribieron el acuerdo de entendimiento el 17 de diciembre de 2025, aunque la firma oficial se realizó en la jornada de Noche Buena.
Según el convenio, NEF debía aportar USD 10 millones como inversión durante 15 años a cambio de asumir la gestión administrativa, financiera y deportiva. Es
[Transcripcion recortada]

El 16 de diciembre asumió el mando el general Ricardo Cajas, comandante de la Fuerza Terrestre del Ejército. Cajas reconoció a PRIMICIAS que sus responsabilidades militares limitaban su tiempo para administrar una institución que ya registraba un déficit de USD 11 millones para finales de 2025.

Un día después de asumir, Cajas firmó un acuerdo de entendimiento con el grupo Naniecheandia SL SA (NEF) para liderar el salvataje. “El club estaba quebrado. Si no tomábamos esa decisión, nos íbamos a Segunda Categoría en ese mismo diciembre”, justificó el dirigente. Sin embargo, la alianza no entregó la solución esperada.

2. La alianza con NEF duró cuatro meses y no 15 años

Cajas y Xiomara Contreras, CEO de Naniecheandia SL SA, suscribieron el acuerdo de entendimiento el 17 de diciembre de 2025, aunque la firma oficial se realizó en la jornada de Noche Buena.

item.title: Man City and their fans did not think this day would come
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Man City and their fans did not think this day would come
2026-09-25
Por Texto propio
Man City and their fans did not think this day would come.
By Sam Lee
Sept. 25, 2026
Friday was the day that Manchester City never seemed to believe would arrive.
Over three and a half years after the Premier League levelled the initial 115 charges at the club, *The Athletic* revealed they have been found guilty of almost all of them.
Punishments are not yet known, which only seems to add to the enormity of the situation: everything appears to be on the table now, from stripped titles to relegation. Even the idea of a fine has become much more serious — surely any financial penalty would be massive.
Lawsuits related to lost earnings for rival teams could take years to resolve, and result in further financial hits. Rival club executives, let alone supporters, will be baying for blood. And what next for the most senior figures, like chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano? Both will be under huge pressure to resign. What about Erling Haaland, and the club's other top stars on long contracts?
Judging by City's response to this kind of thing over the years, it was never supposed to be this way. Ever since the club were first accused of financial wrongdoing in 2018, when *whistleblower Rui Pinto published a tranche of hacked emails*, they have been bullish in the extreme.
When they went to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020 to overturn UEFA's decision to ban them from the Champions League, a picture emerged of former manager Pep Guardiola and the club's top brass, including Soriano, smiling in front of a television screen that bore the news of the club's courtroom triumph. City had not engaged with UEFA's process as they felt it would be prejudiced, so they presented their evidence to CAS instead.
When the Premier League announced its own charges in February 2023, City said they welcomed the opportunity to clear their name and present the "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position", and that has been the line ever since. Given City's victory over UEFA, it always seemed highly possible, if not likely, that the Premier League would be seen off in the same way.

Punishments are not yet known, which only seems to add to the enormity of the situation: everything appears to be on the table now, from stripped titles to relegation. Even the idea of a fine has become much more serious — surely any financial penalty would be massive.

Lawsuits related to lost earnings for rival teams could take years to resolve, and result in further financial hits. Rival club executives, let alone supporters, will be baying for blood. item.title: Why Oracle's force majeure notice is freaking out AI bulls
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why Oracle's force majeure notice is freaking out AI bulls
2026-09-25
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-oracles-force-majeure-notice-is-freaking-out-ai-bulls-170304487.html
Oracle (ORCL) has placed bets across the AI ecosystem, and a new complication could pose problems for the industry.
The tech beast has issued a force majeure notice for its 2.45-gigawatt site in Doña Ana County, N.M., named Project Jupiter, according to a Bloomberg report.
The site is tied to the Stargate initiative with OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) and SoftBank (SFTBY), with OpenAI as the customer. The notice, reportedly sent to the project's developer, private credit player Blue Owl Capital (OWL), is an attempt to delay payments if Project Jupiter fails to go online in 2028.
"Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule. We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward," Oracle vice president Michael Egbert said in a statement to Yahoo Finance. "Force-majeure notices are commonplace in developments of this scale and are often used to preserve contractual rights among project partners. They do not, by themselves, establish a project delay or change delivery expectations."
Oracle stock tanked 4% on the news in Thursday's trading. The development cast a dark cloud over the AI space, sending shares of Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Micron (MU) lower.
"Oracle is in the most tenuous of cash positions of all the major hyperscalers," KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader said. "These types of issues might spread, but Oracle does feel it more acutely than its larger, more cash-rich peers."
Issues spreading is the key concern here, as Oracle has inked scores of deals and taken on enormous amounts of debt to fund its artificial intelligence ambitions. Any disruption to its carefully constructed AI mosaic could make it much harder for Oracle financially, and that means others in the AI space could feel it too.
"By leasing the data centers and getting financing from third parties sometimes the cash payments of the project might be committed to on timelines that do not match the real-world project timeline," Ader continued. "That seems to be what is happening here. Payments might be due on a chronological timeline, but the revenue generation is up to the whims of the complex real-world logistics."

item.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2004 — what it means for stocks: Chart of the Day
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
30-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2004 — what it means for stocks: Chart of the Day
2026-09-25
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/30-year-treasury-yield-hits-highest-level-since-2004--what-it-means-for-stocks-chart-of-the-day-123701823.html
The 30-year Treasury (^TYX) yield rose to its highest level since 2004 on Thursday as stocks fell, raising questions about whether volatility in bond yields could prompt a larger pullback in equities.
The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX), a benchmark for mortgage rates and loans, hovered near its 2007 highs, while the 30-year Treasury yield stood at 5.4% Thursday morning. Meanwhile, stock futures fell.
The move comes as oil prices climbed toward $100 per barrel after President Trump signaled support for a US diesel export ban. Business activity data that came in hotter-than-expected fueled concerns about persistent inflation.
The main driver behind rising rates is "the US economy is booming," Ed Yardeni of Yardeni Research wrote in a note.
Notably, the US dollar has risen to an eight-week high, contributing to downbeat sentiment in just the last couple of days.
"The run-up in the dollar, I think, is associated with negative risk sentiment. And so I think that's affecting equities as well," Steve Englander, co-head of FX Research at Standard Chartered, told Yahoo Finance.
Hawkish remarks from Fed governor Michael Barr also raised expectations of tighter monetary policy among Fed officials. Investors raised their bets on another Fed rate hike in October to 64%.
"There is a sense that the Fed and central banks globally are not willing to tolerate another inflationary shock," Englander added.
A look at a year-to-date chart from Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data shows a steady rise in long-dated bonds as investors price in more Fed rate hikes,
The declines in the stock market so far have been measured. Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC), which posted back-to-back records earlier this week, fell 1% on Wednesday. Most of the declines have centered on interest-rate-sensitive sectors like Utilities (XLU), Real Estate (XLRE), and Financial Services (XLF).
"So far, stocks have continued to shrug off bad news in the most surprising ways," said Dean Lyulkin, president of lending company Cardiff.
The question is whether stocks can keep shrugging off higher rates.
More hikes "could create further strain for already constrained, interest-sensitive sectors while doing little to slow the AI-led investment surge, though it could increase the risk of a stock market correction," EY-Parthenon chief economist Gregory Daco said.
For now, some strategists see small stock market declines as buying opportunities.
"Until US equity indices begin to show more evidence of downside acceleration on this pullback attempt, it's right to consider pullbacks as representing attractive risk/reward opportunities," wrote Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat.

item.title: Paulson is latest Fed official to say more rate hikes may be needed
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Paulson is latest Fed official to say more rate hikes may be needed
2026-09-25
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/paulson-is-latest-fed-official-to-say-more-rate-hikes-may-be-needed-142034400.html
Philadelphia Federal Reserve president Anna Paulson said Thursday that inflation needs attention, which might require further interest rate hikes.
Paulson, a voting member of the rate-setting committee this year, had been in favor of holding rates steady. But she said that by last week's policy meeting, it was clear that underlying inflation wasn't showing signs of coming down.
The Fed's rate hike last week, she said in a speech in Philadelphia, "brings policy closer to what I believe is needed to return inflation to 2% at a pace that balances inflation with risks to the labor market.
"Looking ahead, if conditions evolve as I expect, some modest further tightening may be warranted," Paulson added.
She noted that while tariff-related price pressures have eased, pressures from the conflict in the Middle East and the AI build-out have increased. At the same time, Paulson said she sees a resilient economy that's showing some signs of increased momentum despite tariffs and higher oil prices. She noted that consumer spending has been strong, the AI build-out is driving investment, and the labor market is stable.
"Underlying inflation, however, remains stubbornly elevated," Paulson said. "Against this backdrop, the risk of persistently elevated inflation had increased."
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
Elsewhere, New York Fed president John Williams, who had seemed to believe inflation might be coming down on its own, reportedly said this morning in London, "I don't think the data have suddenly changed on us."
He said AI demand is generating inflation in some sectors, but he is not seeing a broad, cyclical imbalance. When asked about the latest interest rate projections put out by his colleagues, he noted that the median suggested another rate hike may be appropriate by the end of the year.
"That seems to me to be a reasonable way of thinking about it, but we'll have to see," Williams said.
All this comes after Fed governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that further interest rate hikes are needed to bring down sticky inflation.
Markets are moving to price in higher chances of a second rate hike in October, with odds now better than 60%, according to CME Group.

item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The S&P 500 has never been this concentrated in just 2 stocks
2026-09-25
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-sp-500-has-never-been-this-concentrated-in-just-2-stocks-122519280.html
Apple (AAPL) and Nvidia (NVDA) have truly become the straws that stir the stock market's drink.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) has never been more concentrated in just two stocks than it is today, Creative Planning president Peter Mallouk pointed out. Nvidia and Apple represent over 15% of the index (see chart below).
That percentage dusts the 9.1% concentration seen for Microsoft (MSFT) and General Electric (GE) in the lead-up to the dot-com bust.
Nvidia and Apple are on quite a run, which helps to explain their rising importance to the S&P 500.
Apple stock hit $345 on Tuesday, marking an all-time high for the iPhone maker's shares. The stock has come slightly off its highs amid a broader market pullback on rising 10-year US Treasury yields.
The stock has been on a sizzling run since Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 and its first foldable, the Duo, earlier this month, pushing the year-to-date gain to 25%.
Nvidia said in late August that its business stands to grow at least 70% in its next fiscal year. If not for supply constraints, CEO Jensen Huang said growth would be north of 100%.
Shares of the chip giant are up 21% year to date.
Click here for in-depth analysis of the latest stock market news and events moving stock prices

Mortgage rates surge to highest level in over two years: Mortgage and refinance interest rates today
Mortgage rates jumped higher yet again this week as a global bond market selloff intensified.
The average 30-year mortgage rate rocketed 19 basis points to 7.45% by late Thursday, according to Mortgage News Daily, up from 7.26% just a day earlier.
The 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates closely track, has been rising rapidly in recent weeks amid growing investor concern about oil prices, inflation, and future Federal Reserve rate hikes.
On Wednesday, the 10-year yield topped 5.1% to reach a 19-year high, and jumped another 10 basis points on Thursday, to over 5.2%.
"Turmoil in the U.S. Treasury bond market is disrupting plans for shoppers hoping to buy a home at the tail end of the 2026 season, before sellers and buyers pack up for the holidays," Zillow senior economist Kara Ng said in a statement.
Other mortgage rate measures also show the pain. Freddie Mac, which conducts a weekly survey of mortgage rates that can be slower to react to big single-day swings, said the average rate was 7.03% for the week through Wednesday, while the Mortgage Bankers Association calculated the average at 7.12% last week, the highest level since May 2024.

- 7/1 ARM: 6.56%

Use the mortgage calculator below to see how various mortgage rates will impact your monthly payments.
You can bookmark the Yahoo Finance mortgage payment calculator and keep it handy for future use, as you shop for homes and lenders. item.title: Will Social Security go broke in 2032? Congressional Budget Office says benefits must be slashed.
item.author: Hal Bundrick; CFP
item.description:
Will Social Security go broke in 2032? Congressional Budget Office says benefits must be slashed.
2026-09-25
Por Hal Bundrick; CFP
https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/will-social-security-go-broke-in-2032-congressional-budget-office-says-benefits-must-be-slashed-130000243.html
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure.
The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has issued a new projection of Social Security's financial capacity to pay full benefits to enrollees, and it paints a bleaker picture than the one released by the program's own trustees.
The 2026 Social Security Trustees' report projected that the retirement trust fund would be depleted in the fourth quarter of 2032, resulting in a 22% cut in benefits at that time.
The CBO's forecast, released Sept. 17, mirrors the 2032 timeline but deepens the benefit reduction to 26%.
"To protect the promise of Social Security, it is important for lawmakers and the Social Security Administration to work together to ensure the trust funds continue to provide financial stability now and for future generations," Frank J. Bisignano, Commissioner of Social Security, said in a June release. The trustees had previously estimated that benefits would be paid through 2033.
Here is what's happening and what needs to be done to save the system every American worker has helped fund.
Read more: What is the retirement age for Social Security, 401(k), and IRA withdrawals?
Social Security may be 'depleted' but not 'broke'
A recent UCLA/Cornell study confirmed the widely held belief that most people think Social Security is going broke and expect "benefits to cease completely" when it does.
What most people don't consider, the research concluded, are the funds continuing to flow into the system.
Even if reserve funds are depleted, American workers will continue to pay into Social Security through payroll taxes deducted from their paychecks each payday. That means Social Security benefits will continue to be paid, but are likely to be reduced.
"Benefits will continue to be payable after reserve depletion, but not in full unless legislative action is taken," the American Academy of Actuaries noted in an analysis of the SSA's trustees report.
Read more: When will I get my Social Security check? Payment schedule for the month.
What are Social Security trust funds?
As Social Security collects payroll taxes, it pays out benefits to retired workers and eligible family members, as well as death and disability benefits. Workers pay 6.2% from their wages, and employers match that amount. Self-employed individuals pay the full 12.4% of Social Security taxes. Both are capped at a maximum wage.
Medicare taxes and benefits are also collected.
If Social Security collects more than is paid out in benefits, the excess is placed in trust fund reserves and invested in Treasurys to pay future benefits.
"When people talk of Social Security 'going bankrupt,' they are (incorrectly or misleadingly) referring to a scenario where the Social Security Trust Fund has no reserves (it has become 'depleted') and tax revenue is insufficient to cover existing benefits obligations," the Roosevelt Institute, a nonprofit think tank, explained in an analysis.
The fact is, Social Security can pay full benefits for a few more years but then faces a "significant, though manageable, funding shortfall," the institute added.
Read more: Do you pay taxes on Social Security?
What is causing the funding shortfall?
In short: Fewer workers are funding more recipients.
In 1960, there were 5.1 workers paying into the system for every Social Security recipient. That ratio fell throughout the 1980s and 1990s, and when the oldest baby boomers turned 62 in 2008, a dramatic decline began.
In 2024, there were 2.7 workers per beneficiary.
With longer lifetimes and fewer workers per Social Se

item.title: Here's what Wall Street thinks of Meta's new smartglass lineup and first Muse 'holdable'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Here's what Wall Street thinks of Meta's new smartglass lineup and first Muse 'holdable'
2026-09-25
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/heres-what-wall-street-thinks-of-metas-new-smartglass-lineup-and-first-muse-holdable-085705955.html
The word "holdable" has entered the tech hardware lexicon, thanks to Meta (META) and its CEO, Mark Zuckerberg.
Meta's Steve Jobs-like surprise at Meta Connect late Wednesday came in the form of the Muse Charm. It's a standalone pocket device built exclusively for voice interaction with the company's new Muse agent, which is currently one of the top-downloaded apps.
Zuckerberg also showcased a major shift toward "Personal Superintelligence" by unveiling a hardware-meets-AI moment in the Meta VR Glasses.
Weighing just 100 grams — roughly one-fifth the weight of Meta's Quest 3 — the $1,299 spatial computing glasses feature 5K micro-OLED displays, tethered puck processing, and native eye-and-hand tracking.
On the smart eyewear front, Meta debuted the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses, starting at an entry-level $249. Joining them are the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses designed purely for open-ear listening and AI voice interaction.
Here are several of Wall Street's reactions to Meta Connect:
KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson: "Meta's opening keynote for Meta Connect demonstrated the company's progress across AI and connected devices. While we have been impressed by the Muse assistant launch, we see opportunity to deepen AI engagement through new glasses form factors (both audio-only and the new VR glasses at $1,299) and the Muse Charm device (which will be available this audio season). Given Meta is demonstrating the power of weaving AI into devices, we believe more investors will also reconsider Meta's ability to participate in the hardware TAM [total addressable market], where glasses alone represent a 2 billion user opportunity."
Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney: "Collectively, we believe these announcements signal a strategic shift as Meta is placing agentic AI, wearable computing, commerce integrations, and privacy infrastructure at the core of its next computing platform, while taking a more selective approach to traditional Metaverse and VR products. Muse over Metaverse is a good thing for META investors. What was missing in Zuckerberg's keynote was any specific update on Muse adoption (tho perhaps it's too early for that) or on traction for Meta Business Agents (which we believe has significant potential based on our analysis and very recent channel checks). We were also hoping for an update on Watermelon, but we only got the statement that it's coming "soon."
JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth: "While it is still early, we believe that Muse has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT."

Zuckerberg also showcased a major shift toward "Personal Superintelligence" by unveiling a hardware-meets-AI moment in the Meta VR Glasses.

Weighing just 100 grams — roughly one-fifth the weight of Meta's Quest 3 — the $1,299 spatial computing glasses feature 5K micro-OLED displays, tethered puck processing, and native eye-and-hand tracking.

On the smart eyewear front, Meta debuted the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses, starting at an entry-level $249. Joining them are the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses designed purely for open-ear listening and AI voice interaction.

Here are several of Wall Street's reactions to Meta Connect:

KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson: "Meta's opening keynote for Meta Connect demonstrated the company's progress across AI and connected devices. While we have been impressed by the Muse assistant launch, we see opportunity to deepen AI engagement through new glasses form factors (both audio-only and the new VR glasses at $1,299) and the Muse Charm device (which will be available this audio season). Given Meta is demonstrating the power of weaving AI into devices, we believe more investors will also reconsider Meta's ability to participate in the hardware TAM [total addressable market], where glasses alone represent a 2 billion user opportunity."

Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney: "Collectively, we believe these announcements signal a strategic shift as Meta is placing agentic AI, wearable computing, commerce integrations, and privacy infrastructure at the core of its next computing platform, while taking a more selective approach to traditional Metaverse and VR products. Muse over Metaverse is a good thing for META investors. What was missing in Zuckerberg's keynote was any specific update on Muse adoption (tho perhaps it's too early for that) or on traction for Meta Business Agents (which we believe has significant potential based on our analysis and very recent channel checks). We were also hoping for an update on Watermelon, but we only got the statement that it's coming "soon."

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth: "While it is still early, we believe that Muse has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT."

item.title: 2 pandas from China are heading to Zoo Atlanta, Chinese President Xi Jinping says
item.author: ABC News; Angeline Jane Bernabe
item.description:
2 pandas from China are heading to Zoo Atlanta, Chinese President Xi Jinping says
2026-09-25
Por ABC News; Angeline Jane Bernabe
https://abcnews.com/GMA/Living/2-pandas-china-heading-zoo-atlanta-chinese-president/story?id=136725874
2 pandas from China are heading to Zoo Atlanta, Chinese President Xi Jinping says
The Zoo Atlanta will be getting two pandas from China.
During his state visit with President Donald Trump on Thursday at the White House, Chinese President Xi Jinping said he is sending two giant pandas to the U.S.
In remarks ahead of his private meeting with Trump, Xi addressed a number of topics before revealing that the pandas will be arriving at the zoo.
"The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and Americans," Xi said. "Here, I have a piece of good news. In a few days, two pandas, Ping-Ping and Fu Shang, will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta, and meet with the American people."
The announcement comes five months after Zoo Atlanta revealed a new International Cooperative Research Agreement on giant panda conservation, initiated between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association.
Zoo Atlanta told ABC News that they will not be sharing the pandas' arrival date and had no further information to share.
Historically, China has used pandas to mark important diplomatic milestones. In 1972, China sent pandas to the U.S. following President Richard Nixon's historic visit to China, symbolizing cross-cultural collaboration between the U.S. and China, according to the Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute.
The first two pandas that were sent in 1972 to the Smithsonian's National Zoo in Washington, D.C., were giant pandas Ling-Ling (a female) and Hsing-Hsing (a male). The pandas produced five cubs, but none of the offspring survived. A second pair of giant pandas arrived in Washington, D.C., in 2000.
In 1996, pandas Bai Yun and Shi Shi arrived at the San Diego Zoo. They produced a panda cub named Hua Mei through artificial insemination, which was the first panda cub to survive in captivity.
Since then, the zoo saw the arrival of another panda and the births of several cubs before the pandas left in 2019 due to a loan agreement ending with the People's Republic of China.
A new loan agreement between China and the San Diego Zoo started again five years later and on Aug. 8, 2024, the San Diego Zoo welcomed two new pandas.
Zoo Atlanta's giant panda era began in 1999 with the arrival of Lun Lun and Yang Yang. The pair successfully welcomed seven cubs before returning to China in 2024, when the zoo's original giant panda loan agreement with China expired in 2024.
While Zoo Atlanta had nothing further to share, its website says that Ping Ping is a male and Fu Shuang is a female. The pandas were born at Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding in China. Ping Ping was born on March 17, 2020, and Fu Shuang was born on Oct. 18, 2020.

item.title: US-China Summit begins with signs that the trade truce will stay in place — for now
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
US-China Summit begins with signs that the trade truce will stay in place — for now
2026-09-25
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/us-china-summit-begins-with-signs-that-the-trade-truce-will-stay-in-place--for-now-163310660.html
The US-China summit got underway in earnest on Thursday with signals from both sides that importers may be able to count on some stability in the trading relationship between the two nations for the coming few months.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Wednesday that the US and China would extend their current trade truce — set to expire in November — by two months as he set up a new early 2027 deadline for continuing trade talks.
The Chinese didn't immediately confirm that extension, but Chinese President Xi Jinping opened the summit with notably conciliatory remarks on trade. He offered his support, according to a translation, for "a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability" as well as increased flights "to facilitate two-way travel and trade."
A two-month extension could be a letdown for some importers who had been hoping for a one-year extension of the trade pact announced last year in South Korea, but the continuation of current tariff rates and rules for the remainder of 2026 could add a measure of stability.
The extension of the truce will last, Bessent said on Fox News, until Jan. 10, 2027, in order to "to give us more time to see what we can do on the economic front." He has also suggested that a bigger deal with China could be hammered out in the months ahead.
He told reporters in Washington on Wednesday, after a meeting with Vice Premier He Lifeng, that the Chinese "came up with the idea of a bigger deal" and suggested that the US is open to it.
Meanwhile, long-term certainty is more elusive, with both sides keeping options for further provocations on the table.
Trump's team is considering new 7.5% tariffs on China around the issue of overcapacity, but has delayed moving forward until after this week's meeting — and perhaps until after the midterm elections amid withering US public opinion of tariffs.
The current US tariffs on China, according to the Yale Budget Lab, net out to a 26.54% effective statutory tariff rate.
A 'more balanced trading relationship'
Bessent and Trump have repeatedly stressed that the US is ambivalent and would be happy with either an extension of current trade agreements or new talks.
President Trump said during an opening ceremony on Thursday at the White House that "our teams have been working to encourage a more balanced trading relationship."
At issue is a one-year truce announced in South Korea last October that included provisions suspending some tariffs and promises from the Chinese government on rare earth exports.

item.title: Oil prices swing as Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia, US said to be negotiating Hormuz deal with Iran
item.author: Jake Conley
item.description:
Oil prices swing as Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia, US said to be negotiating Hormuz deal with Iran
2026-09-25
Por Jake Conley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-prices-swing-as-houthis-claim-strike-on-saudi-arabia-us-said-to-be-negotiating-hormuz-deal-with-iran-153248858.html
Oil prices swing as Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia, US said to be negotiating Hormuz deal with Iran
Oil prices swung on Thursday after news of attacks inside Saudi Arabia and forceful statements from US and Iranian leaders were tempered by reported dealmaking efforts between Washington and Tehran.
Futures on Brent crude (BZ=F), the international benchmark, rose by more than 4% to trade above $108 per barrel, taking back losses over the past few days that had pushed the contract below the key $100 mark, before falling to hold around $105. Those on US WTI crude (CL=F) ticked up by roughly the same margin to trade near $97 before pulling back below $95.
Oil prices originally spiked on Thursday after Yemen's Houthi militant group, which has been engaged in a widening conflict with Saudi Arabia, claimed to have succeeded in a major round of strikes on Saudi military targets. The growing conflict has severely curtailed the kingdom's ability to export oil, threatening to further reduce oil flows out of the Persian Gulf.
That news furthered a price rally originally sparked by forceful comments at the UN General Assembly summit in New York on Wednesday, where Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would continue to refuse to bow to US pressure. Pezeshkian also reaffirmed Tehran's commitment to maintaining its nuclear program.
While Iranian leaders have long insisted the country's nuclear program is only used for producing civilian energy, President Trump and other senior leaders in the White House have made Iran's nuclear capabilities a key red line in the war between the two nations. Trump has repeatedly asserted that Iran "must not have a nuclear weapon."
Trump said in his own comments to the UN that while he was debating whether to "annihilate" Iran, he expects a deal to be made between Washington and Tehran following the US midterm elections.
"I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to," Trump said. "They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election."
Trump's comments were supported on Thursday by reports that US and Iranian negotiators are working toward a phased deal that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened to shipping traffic by Iran in exchange for relief from the US naval blockade of the nation, first reported by Reuters.
That news sent oil prices falling, taking back some of the gains seen earlier in the day.
Yet even with dealmaking potentially back on the table, the global oil market continues to face multiple pressures. The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked to consistent through-traffic, and Houthi attacks have continued to disrupt Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil through the Red Sea. Attacks by the Ukrainian military have further damaged Russia's refining sector.

item.title: Nike ‘regrets’ Karim Benzema talks after cancelling shoot at last minute over striker’s past
item.author: Desconocido
item.description:
Nike ‘regrets’ Karim Benzema talks after cancelling shoot at last minute over striker’s past
2026-09-24
Por Desconocido
https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7625409/2026/09/24/karim-benzema-nike-shoot/?unlocked_article_code=1.DlE.qj7i.PBNEuL5pgZCF&source=whatsappwc
Nike cancelled a scheduled filming session for a campaign advert featuring the former Real Madrid striker Karim Benzema on Wednesday night after the sportswear company decided the footballer did not align with the brand’s values.
The filming had been scheduled to take place in London on Thursday. Sources briefed on the Nike deal, speaking anonymously as they were not authorized to do so publicly on the matter, said that the company had dug deeper into Benzema’s history and concluded that the player’s publicized past would not align with the brand’s values. Those sources declined to provide further details on the specifics of Benzema’s past which contributed to Nike’s decision.
In a statement to
The Athletic
, Nike said: “This project does not reflect a wider relationship between the athlete and Nike. We regret that conversations got this far.”
Benzema, 38, has previously been convicted of complicity in blackmail in a sex-tape scandal that overshadowed his career with the French national team, missing five years of representing his country as the case continued. A Versailles court
gave Benzema a one-year suspended jail sentence and a €75,000 fine in 2021
. This convicted him of “complicity” in an attempt to blackmail France teammate Mathieu Valbuena in 2015. Benzema’s legal team initially said they would appeal but the appeal was abandoned in 2022. His lawyer Hugues Vigier told

Her gender. Her ethnicity. Her electability. Her eggs. Her movement. Her moment.

Ms. Ocasio-Cortez, 36, the youngest woman ever elected to Congress, is now in her eighth year representing parts of the Bronx and Queens. She could simply keep winning re-election. But in 2028, she has two other choices: run for the White House, or seek the seat now held by Senator Chuck Schumer of New York.
“Every element of this is something that’s within consideration,” she said.
Ms. Ocasio-Cortez weighed aloud the pros and cons of running for president with unusual candor, sounding less strategic than searching, as if the right answer were somewhere nearby.
“Bloat check!”
) about fertility treatments preparing for a possible future pregnancy.
“I think about it personally,” she said of a White House run. “I am 36, I’m about to turn 37 years old — and what that means for my life.”
“Pretty candidly, I think about my identity,” Ms. Ocasio-Cortez went on. “I’m not naïve to the fact that we are living under a very regressive administration, and I happen to be a woman, and I, you know, happen to be Latina. And I think that there’s a lot of conversation about electability, and I don’t kind of shy away from those realities.”
Ms. Ocasio-Cortez arrived in Congress as a left-wing outsider and remains one of the party’s most progressive voices. Some party strategists are urging
Democrats to move to the middle
. But Ms. Ocasio-Cortez was heartened by “the ascendance for the first time” of progressives like Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan who toppled big-money candidates in this year’s Senate primaries.
“I have a tremendous amount of fear over the corruption of our political system,” she said.
She spoke by phone last week as she recovered in her Washington apartment from Covid. She had called
to discuss an upcoming swing through upstate New York and a cash transfer
to help Democrats in her home state.

item.title: Xi Jinping appears to be leaving China's CEOs at home for his Washington trip
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Xi Jinping appears to be leaving China's CEOs at home for his Washington trip
2026-09-24
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/xi-jinping-appears-to-be-leaving-chinas-ceos-at-home-for-his-washington-trip-155540891.html
As recently as last week, Chinese President Xi Jinping was expected to arrive in Washington with a large delegation of Chinese CEOs, as President Trump touted a dealmaking atmosphere surrounding the two leaders' summit.
Now, Xi is scheduled to arrive this evening with a significantly smaller business delegation in tow, dampening expectations even as an array of US executives remains set to be on hand for the gathering.
Chinese state media announced Xi's departure for the US on Wednesday, noting only a small entourage that included family members and political aides.
The South China Morning Post reported that a lack of progress on deals had led to the paring back of the list from the Chinese side.
US industry leaders had been expecting a wide array of Chinese business leaders to be in attendance from electric car makers and agriculture companies.
A White House official didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday. Trump's team previously confirmed Thursday's state dinner would include Sam Altman of OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), Jensen Huang of Nvidia (NVDA), and Elon Musk of Tesla (TSLA).
The summit is set to begin this evening, when Trump will travel to Joint Base Andrews to greet Xi when he arrives at 6 p.m. ET.
The tone shift around business deals comes as other policy areas like AI and trade are expected to see only small steps forward, and signs emerge that Trump is set to roll out the red carpet for the Chinese leader.
Close observers of US-China relations have noted that Xi did not do the same when Trump visited Beijing in May, sending a subordinate for Trump's arrival.
Some of the US CEOs set to attend this week's festivities, including Huang and Musk, traveled with Trump to Beijing earlier this year.
Members of both leaders' economic teams are set to be in attendance, including US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, who met in New York over the weekend.
Bessent left that meeting describing the talks as constructive and saying the US had proposed a new AI safety "notification mechanism" that could allow Bessent and He and other officials to communicate quickly in the event of an incident related to AI. But China has yet to publicly embrace the idea.
The lack of further progress on AI underscored the modest ambitions of this week's summit that might be high on pomp and circumstance but light on policy.
There is little expectation of the US or China agreeing to broader limits on AI, such as regulating frontier models. In fact, both sides have signaled that they are eager to race forward with the technology.
Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.
Read the latest financial and business news from Yahoo Finance

item.title: Dollar jumps to near two-month high on Fed outlook, inflation concern
item.author: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.description:
Dollar jumps to near two-month high on Fed outlook, inflation concern
2026-09-24
Por Chuck Mikolajczak
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/currencies/articles/dollar-holds-near-2-month-014317337.html
By Chuck Mikolajczak
NEW YORK, Sept 23 (Reuters) - The US dollar rallied to its highest level in nearly two months on Wednesday as investors' expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike grew, while oil prices jumped after Iran cast doubt on progress in peace talks.
Since the central bank's rate hike of 25 basis points last week to the 3.75%-4.00% range, several Federal Reserve officials have flagged the possibility of more rate increases if inflation does not cool.
On Wednesday, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the US central bank took an important step last week to "recalibrate" short-term borrowing costs to bring down inflation, and will likely need to deliver further interest rate hikes.
"It's a rate story right now," said Elias Haddad, global head of markets strategy at Brown Brothers Harriman in London.
"What's driving the dollar higher is a follow through from the hawkish Fed hike that we got last week and that's just given the dollar some renewed momentum. This week there hasn't been much data, or policy relevant data, but what was interesting is the comments from Fed officials, they're basically all toeing the same line that more tightening is in the pipeline."
The dollar extended gains after S&P Global said its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, increased to 58.4 this month, its highest since July 2021, after a 56.0 reading in August, powered by a surge in new orders, though strong demand strained supply chains and pushed prices higher.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.51% to 101.06 after hitting 101.23, its highest since July 29.
Expectations the Fed will hike rates by at least 25 basis points at its October meeting climbed after the data and were last at about 70%, according to LSEG data, up from roughly 53% before the release.
MIDDLE EAST TENSIONS LIFT OIL
Further fueling gains in the greenback was a rise in oil prices, after Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said in an interview with state TV that as long as Iran's conditions are not met, the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened and there would be no negotiations.
In addition, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran and the United States remain far apart on how to end their war but diplomacy must continue, after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
Hopes that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly could lead to a resolution to the seven-month-long Iran war had helped push oil prices lower since reaching a four-month high in mid-September, but have since reversed course this week.

item.title: US fixed 30-year mortgage rate jumps to 7.12%, MBA says
item.author: Ann Saphir
item.description:
US fixed 30-year mortgage rate jumps to 7.12%, MBA says
2026-09-24
Por Ann Saphir
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/us-fixed-30-mortgage-rate-110217949.html
By Ann Saphir
Sept 23 (Reuters) - The rate on the most popular US home loan rose last week to its highest in more than two years, after the Federal Reserve lifted short-term interest rates to combat inflation, and rising oil prices drove up Treasury yields that underpin residential borrowing costs.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage jumped 15 basis points to 7.12% in the week ended September 18, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in May 2024.
Mortgage rates have risen more than a full percentage point since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began pushing up the global price of oil in late February, putting the squeeze on prospective homebuyers and a chill into the US housing market.
Mortgage rates track US Treasury yields, which are sensitive to oil prices and the threat they pose to inflation, which has been running above the Fed's 2% goal for 5-1/2 years.
Last week the Fed increased its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range to put inflation on a "timelier" path to 2%, and nearly all Fed policymakers projected at least one more rate increase by the end of this year. Traders are also betting on further Fed rate hikes.
The rise in mortgage rates last week led to a decline in refinancing and home purchase applications, the MBA said, and drove more borrowers into adjustable-rate mortgages, which offer lower upfront borrowing costs than fixed-rate mortgages and reset after a number of years to whatever the going rate is at the time. ARMs accounted for 9.8% of mortgage applications last week, the MBA said.
(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Chris Reese)
